If I could give 0 stars, I absolutely would.

This was genuinely the worst experience I have ever had with any food establishment.

We placed an order at 8:24pm and did not receive our food until approximately 10pm. During this time we were forced to visit the store on THREE separate occasions due to alleged system errors and confusion over whether our order existed, despite having already paid.

We were left waiting outside in extremely hot weather with a young baby who was distressed, hungry and in need of feeding.

The most shocking part of the evening was the behaviour of the manager, Abbas, who was hostile, aggressive and shouted at us in the store whilst we were simply trying to collect food we had already paid for. We were incorrectly told we would need to pay again and were spoken to in a completely unacceptable and unprofessional manner.

After further calls, the store later admitted there had in fact been an error on their side, yet no apology was ever offered.

When we finally collected our food on the third visit, staff simply handed over boxes without checking the contents and the manager did not even have the courtesy to come and speak to us.

When we arrived home, we discovered the order was wrong anyway.

We ordered a Thin Crust pizza but received a Classic Crust pizza instead. We are fully aware of the difference between the two and can confirm that the wrong product was supplied.

Even more concerning, we received a pizza containing ham and pepperoni which we had not ordered. This raises serious concerns regarding order accuracy, food preparation procedures, contamination risks and quality control within the store.

Despite raising these concerns formally, the response received was dismissive and appeared to avoid responsibility rather than address the issues raised.

After years of ordering from Papa John’s, this experience has completely destroyed our confidence in the brand. We will not be returning and will be taking our business elsewhere.

If I could give 0 stars, I would.

I ordered a thin crust pizza over the phone. When I received my order at around 5:07 PM, I was given an original pizza instead. I called the store at 5:10 PM to explain the issue. The staff member told me that the pizza was thin crust, but as a regular customer, I politely explained that I know the difference between a thin crust and an original pizza.

During the conversation, the call was disconnected. Since I did not receive a callback, I called again. I was then told that the pizza could not be remade, but that I would receive an extra side item for free on my next order.

My complaint is not about receiving free food or compensation. I understand that mistakes can happen. What disappointed me was the way the situation was handled. The response I received felt dismissive, and there was no effort to properly resolve the issue or acknowledge the mistake. The main issue for me was that the call appeared to be ended while I was still speaking politely and trying to explain the situation.

I am not happy with the customer service I received. The staff member said her name was Regina (although I am not sure if that was correct). I hope this feedback helps improve customer service and how similar situations are handled in the future.

I've been a loyal Kärcher owner for many years. My current machine, a K5, was purchased four years ago.

At some point, Kärcher's R&D department decided it would be a good idea to replace their excellent pressure hoses with an utterly dreadful design. Not only are they a nightmare to coil up and store, they kink at the slightest opportunity. The result? Constant pressure loss and the ridiculous sight of me having to walk the hose out in a straight line just to remove the kinks and restore performance.

What I didn't expect was Kärcher's response when it became obvious they'd got it wrong.

Rather than openly acknowledge the problem and support existing customers, they quietly introduced a new kink-free hose while saying very little about the shortcomings of the old one. When I visited a Kärcher service centre to buy one, I was told a 10-metre replacement hose would cost more than £60.

Frankly, Kärcher should have replaced these grossly substandard hoses free of charge. With annual revenues of around €3.5 billion and healthy profits, they could easily have afforded to look after loyal customers and preserve the goodwill that built their reputation.

Instead, they chose not to.

I had little choice but to buy the replacement hose, but Kärcher's handling of this issue has cost them a customer. When my K5 eventually reaches the end of its life, I won't be buying another Kärcher.

I'll be buying an AVA pressure washer instead. That much is guaranteed.

I found the whole experience deeply disappointing and, from a customer's perspective, lacking in transparency.

The vehicle was advertised at £21,750, which prompted my enquiry. I then spent time reviewing videos, checking the specification and carrying out detailed due diligence before deciding whether to travel to view the car.

During those discussions, the advertised price suddenly increased by almost £3,700 to £25,499.

I was subsequently told this was due to a "technical glitch" and that the vehicle had been listed before the pricing team had reviewed it. Whether that explanation is accepted or not, the end result is the same: a customer invests their time based on one advertised price only to find the price has increased significantly while discussions are ongoing.

That is not the level of transparency or ethical business practice I expect from a large national dealership. It leaves the impression that advertised prices cannot be relied upon and that the goalposts can move without warning after a customer has already engaged.

I have therefore decided to take my business elsewhere. I would advise other buyers to exercise caution and confirm that any advertised price will actually be honoured before investing their own time in making enquiries or travelling to view a vehicle.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with the level of customer service I received from Porsche Nottingham. Having chosen a Porsche dealership, I expected a premium experience that reflected the reputation of the brand, but unfortunately, my experience was the complete opposite.

From the outset, communication was poor. I repeatedly had to chase for updates, as nobody seemed willing to keep me informed without prompting. Phone calls and emails were either ignored or responded to far later than expected, leaving me constantly wondering what was happening. For a dealership representing a luxury manufacturer, this lack of communication is simply unacceptable.

What frustrated me most was the attitude of some of the staff. Rather than making me feel like a valued customer, I felt like I was an inconvenience. There was very little effort to listen to my concerns or provide clear explanations, and I often felt that I was being brushed aside rather than helped. Customer service should be about building trust and confidence, but I left feeling completely let down.

The overall organisation also seemed poor. I encountered unnecessary delays, conflicting information depending on who I spoke to, and a general lack of ownership of my queries. It often felt like nobody was prepared to take responsibility for resolving issues, meaning I had to spend my own time chasing progress and repeating the same information to different members of staff.

When customers choose Porsche, they are paying not only for an exceptional vehicle but also for an exceptional ownership experience. Sadly, Porsche Nottingham failed to deliver on either the professionalism or the customer care that I expected. Instead of feeling valued, I left feeling frustrated, disappointed, and questioning whether customer satisfaction is genuinely a priority.

I sincerely hope the dealership takes this feedback seriously, invests in improving communication, staff training, and accountability, and begins treating customers with the level of respect and professionalism that the Porsche name represents. Based on my experience, I would struggle to recommend Porsche Nottingham to others.

First impressions are everything !

And my first impression of parkland motors was very disappointing, I came to view a car that had placed a deposit on the day before so parkland knew I was coming!
So after arriving I was told someone would be with me Shortly, After (10/15) mins someone came over to me and said I’m going to give you the keys so you can have a look at the car yourself !
Having gone to have a look around the car I spotted the tyre was flat and there wasn’t a drop a diesel in the tank , so I went back into the showroom to mention the couple of issues . Was told someone would get on it asap ! ( half hour later ) the tyre had been fixed , then was told Someone was going to have to get some diesel before I could take it for a little test drive (another 15 mins later )

So after 1 hr I was still waiting to take the car for a test drive , which in all honesty Is a very poor experience so far considering the company knew I was coming as I’d arranged a time the day before, I think the car should have been ready for me ! But eh what do I know ?
Anyway took car for a drive and loved it so decided to go ahead with the purchase !

Now this is where it all gets very interesting ,
After a couple of issues with sensors flagging up on dashboard , I contacted the  parkland garage and to be fair to them they took the car back in and fixed the issues ( I had 3 months warranty )
So was covered obviously !

After my warranty ended I was starting to hear grinding /rubbing noises coming form the front wheels when I was braking , so took the car to my local garage who came back to me and told me that it needed new pads but more importantly the brake shins were missing !
Having no knowledge of this the garage told me or asked me where I got the car from and told me that who ever did the previous work on my car had not done the work to a satisfactory standard it should be ( basically cut corners by not adding the brake shins back on when they had fitted pads on the car)
The reason I know that it was parkland at fault for this poor workmanship was because the car had come with paperwork to say it had been fully serviced(see paperwork with information of brake pads & discs being fitted) and a full car check !

Which let’s be honest anyone can sign a piece of paperwork to say something has been done , but clearly hadn’t!

Now after I’d spoken to my local garage they told me to contact parkland to see what they were prepared to do about it ! They also said any reputable or decent car garage would put things right and fix it free of charge !

Guess what ??
Parkland didn’t come under that category of decent car garages , I phone parkland left a few details explained the situation, someone told me I’d be contacted in The next 24 hrs once the team looked into the issue , didn’t hear anything for at 3/4 days , so decided to contact them again and finally got to speak to someone at parkland, that persons name was ASH , he wasn’t prepared to listen , he was very arrogant ( he went on to say that the brake shins that was missing didn’t need to be fitted to the car , and that there was no way to prove that they wasn’t missing before they had the car in their hands) and basically said that they wasn’t prepared to sort the issue!

All I’m going to say is to anyone who has read this , please if your going to buy a car from parkland , make sure you get it checked over by another garage while your warranty is still in date , and also make sure you don’t deal with ash the car salesman/head mechanic/human resources lead/toilet cleaner/valet cleaner/man of many skills but clearly best at lying and just be a genuine see you next Tuesday kinda guy !!!!

I would like to raise a formal concern regarding my daughter's recent check-up appointment with Dr Mohammed Saeed at Collegiate Dental Practice.

This was the first time we had been seen by this dentist. Unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing and fell well below the standard of patient care and communication I would expect, particularly when treating a child.

At the start of the appointment, Dr Saeed did not introduce himself, greet either myself or my daughter, or make any effort to make us feel welcome. There was very little communication throughout the appointment. He simply stated that my daughter needed X-rays and asked me to wait outside. Once the X-rays had been completed, I was not called back into the room and was left to assume I should return when I noticed the door had been left ajar.

During the examination itself, there was no explanation of what was being done, what he was looking for, or what he had found. My daughter was not spoken to in a reassuring manner, nor was any effort made to put her at ease. He did not check whether she was comfortable, explain procedures before carrying them out, or ask whether she was experiencing any pain or discomfort.

My daughter told me afterwards that her mouth was hurting during the examination and that the instruments repeatedly caught the inside of her mouth and skin, causing discomfort. She flinched several times as a result. What concerns me most is that despite these visible reactions, there was no pause to ask if she was okay, no acknowledgement that she appeared uncomfortable, and no reassurance given. The examination simply continued without any communication regarding her discomfort.

The examination also felt quite rough, which added to my daughter's distress. As a parent, I found it concerning that there appeared to be so little awareness of, or attention to, her comfort and wellbeing throughout the appointment.

At the end of the appointment, there was no explanation of the findings, no summary of the check-up, and no opportunity to ask questions. The only advice given was not to eat for 30–40 minutes. The chair was then put upright and the appointment effectively ended without any indication that the examination was complete, nor was there any goodbye or discussion regarding future care.

While I appreciate that clinical qualifications and technical skills are important, patient care, communication, professionalism and empathy are equally important, especially when treating children. My daughter left the appointment feeling uncomfortable and upset, and I left feeling dissatisfied with the level of care and communication we received.

I would appreciate it if this feedback could be formally recorded and passed on. I would also request that my daughter is not booked with Dr Mohammed Saeed for any future appointments.

I look forward to receiving a response regarding this matter.

I was extremely concerned and upset to discover that my son had been placed on a waiting list with Mantle Psychology without my knowledge or consent. As his primary carer, I would have expected to be contacted and involved before any referral relating to autism or other developmental assessments was progressed.

Learning that my child had been referred for assessment without my awareness was distressing. These are significant matters that can have a lasting impact on a child's life, and I believe parents should be appropriately informed and involved throughout the process wherever possible.

What added to my concerns was that the referral appeared to originate through a professional connection involving my son's father's current partner, who works within the organisation. This raised questions for me about how the referral was handled and whether appropriate safeguards were followed.

I was also surprised by the speed at which my son appeared to be added to the waiting list, particularly given comments from others regarding lengthy waiting times. While I appreciate that every case is different, the circumstances left me with questions about the process.

To be fair, when I contacted the practice to raise my concerns, I received a prompt and professional response, and my son was removed from the waiting list quickly. I am grateful for the way my email was handled.

However, the overall experience left me feeling excluded from an important decision concerning my child's care and wellbeing. I hope the practice will review its procedures to ensure that all individuals with parental responsibility are appropriately informed and involved when referrals of this nature are made.

I brought the car to GAC in mid April for review of an engine rattle together with the EPC and engine management lights, which I suspected were timing-chain related. They diagnosed a stretched timing chain that had jumped, quoted £2,300 for a full replacement, and I approved that work on the clear understanding that it would resolve the symptoms I presented with.
After the timing chain was replaced, they said the timing was now correct— yet the rattle persisted exactly as before, and the EPC light comes on intermittently. At that point, they advised replacing the cam bridge gauze (which they inspected and said was faulty), and I reluctantly approved the additional £500 which i had to borrow, because I needed the car urgently and trusted their expertise as a German car specialist.
Despite that second intervention, the rattle has not been resolved. They then suggested the inlet camshaft “might” need replacing for a further £2,000. At this stage I declined any more work, as the original problems have not been fixed after £2,900 spent and multiple stages of parts replacement.
While I accept that complex engine issues on these TFSI engines can sometimes reveal additional faults once the primary timing problem is addressed, the core issue I paid to have resolved — the persistent engine rattle and intermittent EPC light — remains as well as the Engine Warning light.. In my view, this goes beyond a reasonable “step-by-step diagnostic approach.” The work carried out has not delivered the repair I was led to expect, and the symptoms that brought the car in are still present.
You have suggested that further work on the vehicle can be done for an additional £1000 as a compromise which MAY resolve the issue. Unfortunately, I do not have an inexhaustible amount of funds and had I know the parts cannon approach was going to be adopted from Day 1, I would have taken my business elsewhere. Hindsight is a wonderful thing. If you're a gambling person who likes to roll the dice with your vehicle, by all means chance your luck with this outfit. As for myself, I'm out of pocket to the tune of nearly £3000 with the vehicle as problematic with warning lights lighting up my display as before.
I have no choice but to seek independent legal advice and pursue a formal remedy, which may include a partial refund of the £2,900+ or through the Motor Ombudsman / small claims process. What a bloody headache.

During my time living there a security guard named Joe used his master key to enter my flat in the middle of the night, the lights in the flat were out but luckily 2 of my flatmates were awake on their phones in the living room. I had just gone to my room to get ready to sleep. He entered the flat without knocking or making his presence known. Me and my flatmate at the time were part of the universities pole fitness society and we had a pole set up in our communal space. Joe entered our living room and upon hearing my flatmates (both girls) talking to a man I joined them in the living room to see what was happening. Joe said he’d seen the pole from the courtyard and wanted to come and look. He asked which of my housemates were the ones who used it and then requested that we invited him over the next time we were practicing.
We asked him to leave as we all felt uncomfortable. We reported the incident to management who initially stated they would take it seriously. They later came back having conducted an “investigation” where they claimed joe had entered our flat based on a noise complaint some other residents had put in about our flat specifically. When we asked to see some evidence (cctv or otherwise) they could not provide it. Joe mentioned no noise complaint whatsoever and stated his reason for being there was the pole. They then interrogated me and my flatmates in separate interviews about our version of events and shifted the focus to our pole. When I claimed it was not a permanent structure and would cause no damage whatsoever to the flat they organised a maintenance visit to inspect it.
Their outcome for this situation was that Joe had to undertake an online “ethics in the workplace” course and he still worked as security of the ppq buildings, I had to see him regularly even after he knew we reported him . My outcome is that 5 years later, at the age of 24 I cannot sleep if I am alone in my house.
In hindsight I should have pushed harder with the police at the time of this incident.
I wouldn’t recommend anyone living here on the basis that if something goes wrong they will protect their staff over the safety of the students.

Medical care should come first, making a profit second.

Because the car was fresh in stock, the physical paperwork wasn't available, but I was allowed to take a photo of the service history from their computer screen.
Upon reviewing the photo later that day, I noticed the car had missed a service interval by 10,000 miles. As this voids the manufacturer’s 8-year battery warranty, I immediately emailed them (just hours after paying the deposit) to state I would not be proceeding and politely requested my refund, as agreed.
On 26 April, the branch manager called me and explicitly confirmed that my deposit would be returned.
Unfortunately, that was the last proactive communication I received. After the funds failed to arrive, I emailed their advice team on 11 May. I was told my email was forwarded to the Rochdale branch manager. Hearing nothing back, I called the branch on 14 May. The receptionist was aware of my case and said management would call me back. They did not.
As of writing this, I am still waiting for the refund that was guaranteed at the point of sale and confirmed by the manager. Based on my experience, I strongly advise against leaving any deposit with this branch unless you are absolutely certain you are buying the car, as getting your money back seems to be an incredibly frustrating and drawn-out process.

Very poor aftercare and complaint handling from DFS Nottingham.

We bought a large ivory sofa from this store less than 3 years ago, costing approximately £1,600, along with SofaCare and DFS cleaning products. At the point of sale, the aftercare process was explained as: try the recommended products first, then alternative products if needed, then a technician clean, and only then replacement covers if required.

After using the DFS-recommended cleaning products, the sofa has developed visible water/tide marks over time. The sofa is otherwise structurally sound and comfortable, but the fabric now looks visibly marked and its value has been affected.

When I raised this, I received a phone call saying DFS were not aware of this issue unless too much product had been used, while also saying they were not accusing me of that. I was then offered replacement cushion covers at a discounted price of £35 each. I asked for the matter to be escalated as a formal complaint and for everything to be put in writing.

I explained that my complaint is not simply about needing new covers — it is that the SofaCare/cleaning products were sold as the correct aftercare route, and following that advice has left the sofa marked. DFS replied that the products are tested and offered the discounted covers again, which did not address the complaint.

I asked for a proper financial remedy, such as free replacement covers, a partial refund/price reduction, goodwill payment, or a final response letter. DFS then suggested a technician assessment, which I agreed to promptly because I am leaving the country in the first week of July. Since then I have had further phone calls but no proper written confirmation of the appointment, no clear purpose for the visit, and no complaint resolution. I was also told the technician may be able to price replacement parts, which is not what I am looking for — I am not paying for parts after following DFS’s recommended care process.

The handling has been slow, unclear and extremely frustrating. I have repeatedly asked for everything in writing and stressed the urgency, but I still do not have a proper resolution or final position.

In hindsight, the poor service started at the point of sale, when the finance application was put through with the wrong date of birth. I would not buy from this store again.

1 star – in the hope that someone will take this feedback on board.

Overall, this is a good church with strong biblical teaching, engaging speakers, and an excellent worship team. However, despite its many strengths, I found it surprisingly difficult to become part of the community.

I signed up to join a small group but never received a response. From what I could see, these groups also only run for around eight weeks, making it difficult to build lasting relationships. As a large church, it can already feel intimidating to navigate socially if you don't know anyone, so having limited opportunities for meaningful connection is disappointing.

I'm also surprised that a church so committed to growth doesn't offer a structured, in-person programme for newcomers. A dedicated New Joiners course or welcome pathway would make a huge difference in helping people feel seen, supported, and connected.

Another area that felt overlooked was ministry for single or unmarried women. There are initiatives such as Motherhood Mornings and Men's Prayer Nights, but I couldn't find any equivalent space for young unmarried women. It feels like this demographic has been unintentionally overlooked, despite it being a significant part of the congregation.

My intention isn't to criticise the church's teaching or leadership, both of which I value, but to highlight areas where I believe the church could better support those who are new and looking for genuine community. I hope this feedback is received in the constructive spirit in which it is intended.

Gethair doesn't provide good service or a good end result.  I had a hair transplant years ago with this company unfortunately the result was very bad.

Secondly you knew about this condition and assured me you could still proceed and get a good result..  I have since used another hair transplant clinic which unlike yours is competent, honest and professional. DO NOT ORDER TIMBER FROM B&Q
I ordered timber from B&Q as an essential component of a polytunnel build. From the outset, the experience was poor — it took a week just to receive a delivery date, which fell on a Sunday during a bank holiday weekend. When I requested an alternative, the next available slot was the following Sunday, as apparently they only deliver on Sundays.
The Friday before the rescheduled delivery — after my partner and I had already booked Monday and Tuesday off work to assemble the tunnel — B&Q sent me an email notification of a partial refund. No explanation. No warning. When I checked against my plans, I discovered they had silently reduced the quantity of timber in my order. The specific lengths I'd ordered for the frame had been cut, meaning the polytunnel could not be built.
Had I not investigated the partial refund myself, B&Q would have turned up on Sunday, dumped over £100 worth of timber outside my house, and left me with materials that were completely insufficient to complete the project. Meanwhile, plants that depend on the polytunnel for protection are now at risk of dying.
I called customer service. They offered nothing — no solution, no alternative, no urgency. When I demanded compensation for the wasted time off work, I was told they couldn't even look at a compensation claim until the refund had been processed, which wouldn't be until the end of the following week.
I have spent significant money at B&Q on this project. This is the worst customer experience I have ever had with any retailer — not just inconvenient but actively costly. I've cancelled the order and I will never shop at B&Q again.

I had a disappointing experience with these landlords. While they present themselves online as highly successful, my experience as a tenant didn’t reflect that level of professionalism.

Maintenance issues were often handled slowly and sometimes only after repeated follow-ups. For example, a mould issue I reported took a long time to be addressed, which I found stressful and concerning from a health perspective.

In my experience, the property was rarely, if ever, visited or inspected by the landlords. I also felt that shared spaces and general house management were not well controlled, which created a difficult living environment at times.

During my tenancy, I observed situations that suggested rooms may have been overcrowded, and I felt there was limited management oversight. Cleaners and contractors did attend, but in my opinion the quality of work was inconsistent.

I was also asked to show prospective tenants around the property, which I found unusual, and I was aware that some tenants were offered referral incentives, although this was never offered to me.

Based on my personal experience, I wouldn’t choose to rent from them again.

one_star_reviews.text:
In a Facebook post posted by the Dome on the 30th of April 2025, they claim that they are the “biggest gym in their group”. With this comes the expectation that the gym would be well kept in order to keep up with high demand from consumers amongst Doncaster. However, from my experiences, I can say this is particularly false.

To begin, the free weights zone is below adequate gym standards, with an outdated and poorly maintained air conditioning unit, causing the area to be constantly boiling, which as been recently unbearable in the 30⁰C temperatures outside the gym. Alongside this, equipment is unsafe and obsolete. In particular, there are 2 squat racks, a hammer strength and another brand. The hammer strength squat rack has a sticker on it saying how it is "not safe for use", despite everyone still using it, showing how the Dome has little care for the maintenance of equipment alongside the safety of customers. This other brand of squat rack no longer exists, and lots of people refuse to use it because it looks unsafe. The Dome could remove this particular piece of equipment and add in a piece of equipment that consumers have been asking to have in this area for a long time such as a t-bar row, which would only cost 0.00775% of the Dome's recent investment into their swimming facilities, yet they refuse to add it, showing how the Dome refuses to meet consumer demands just to remain at status quo.

As well as this, the pressure on the water fountain within the gym is extremely low, where it takes about 2 minutes to fill a litre bottle. This is below the minimum standard and should be a priority to fix for any form of health facility.

Furthermore, I have spotted mould on the ceilings of the gym, specifically above the squat rack, which is a clear indicator of failure to manage moisture, humidity, and airflow in an environment already prone to dampness, showing a lack of care for maintenance by senior staff.

Finally, the steam room is poorly maintained and kept. It consistently smells of faeces and one time me and a couple of others who I went in with saw brown stains on the walls. We were promised investigations into why the steam room was not being cleaned but nothing has changed. Additionally, the changing rooms always has a smell of mould and the water pressure on the showers is poor.

I believe that if you are looking for a gym where they care about health and safety, as well as cleanliness, do not look into the Dome gym and please look at other alternatives in Doncaster such as commercial brands like JD and The Gym Group. These parallel the Dome in price, the Gym group coming in at a starting price of £20 a month and JD, despite the more premium price of £30 a month is still less than the sub-par hygiene package that the Dome gym offers. I would also recommend other DCLT branches that have recently undergone refurbishment such as Balby, as you are getting a much better deal, without having to change memberships.

One benefit of privatising DCLT would be the ability for them to make supernormal profits. This is because them acting as a charity means they have to “reinvest” their revenue back into the leisure facilities (meaning manager’s pockets) rather than profiting. This means there is a lack of dynamic efficiency for DCLT as they do not bother to upgrade their facilities, rather they let them rot as there is consumer inertia, where DCLT consumers are inert and do not want to switch gyms, making the demand for their facilities inelastic. This has allowed DCLT to get away with charging outrageous prices for their subpar facilities, robbing consumers of allocative efficiency, while clearly having a huge X-inefficiency of failing to minimise costs for the £25.8 million “investment” that was an overspend of over £11 million. The council raiding funds for other areas of Doncaster such as the adult social care fund and the Covid fund to bail out DCLT highlights significant government failure as well as information failure as people do not know about the negative externalities associated with DCLT.

DCLT receives millions in bailouts from the council who also raids hundreds of thousands of pounds from the pots of the Covid fund, the social care fund, and the family fund to bail out the Dome, wastes our taxpayer money, despite it being a ‘not for profit’ it is in dire need of being privatised to give back to the people that have been inputting money to the dome for nearly 40 years. They claim the Dome generates “social value” but this is PR nonsense to distract us from the fact that they make a loss of £4 million per year and get bailed out by the taxpayers for no benefit to them. The public nature removes responsibility from the dome to improve services, such as the gym, as they know they will be bailed out.

The gym is out of date, some machines are almost always broken, one was for nearly half a year, dumbbells have visible rust on them and some of the rubber casting on the weight has fallen off. the only good area is the freeweight section and that is still lacking. I’d personally recommend new plates, and new equipment like an incline bench and some more row variations like chest supported T bar row. Not to mention the changing rooms, showers without heads, and the smell in there and the steam room is unbearable. I tried to put in an enquiry about the sorry state of the gym but have still received no reply.

TLDR;

Staff that care about fitness and not making a quick buck ❌
Good equipment ❌
Good management ❌
Cares about customers ❌
Mismanaged funding that doesn’t go to the gym ✅
Terrible water pressure ✅
Poorly maintained equipment and plates so old that the rubber is falling off of them ✅
Millions in bailouts of taxpayer money ✅

Should you come here? Only if they make the proper improvements soon, but right now I’d advise against it.

Gutted to be writing this review. I’m on maternity leave and finally plucked up the courage to do something for myself to try and gain back a little confidence. I purchased the £15 two‑session trial so I could attend the Beginners Pole Level 1 & 2 on Monday evenings.

The first class was cancelled with an apology email and text just after 4pm on the day. No reason was given, but I was able to rebook for the following two Mondays. Alix offered to move me to an aerial class later that evening, but that didn’t fit in with home commitments and wasn’t what I had booked.

The next Monday came and, again just after 4pm, I received another cancellation email. This time it was due to a shoulder injury. I was again offered the aerial class, which was still not what I had booked and again at an unsuitable time.

I emailed Alix to say I was unable to attend anything other than the 6:15pm class and that I was now also unable to transfer to the following two weeks as the package was only valid for three weeks. I received no response. I followed up with a text — no response. I then sent a message via the website later in the week — still no response. I also wanted to confirm whether the class would be running on the bank holiday.

On Monday 4th, at 3pm, I received yet another email stating the class was cancelled. No reason was given this time, and no alternative offered. I emailed again asking for a full refund, as I had completely lost faith in this studio. I have since submitted a chargeback request to my bank.

Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, a refund cannot be withheld if the company is unable to uphold the contract. Unfortunately, that has been my experience here: repeated last‑minute cancellations, poor communication, and no resolution.

Posted on behalf of my wife.

The decor, presentation, and overall vibe of the restaurant are genuinely impressive. Unfortunately, that’s where the positives end.

There was a constant buzzing sound coming from one of the speakers that the staff were unable to resolve. It completely affected the atmosphere for my friends and me, making it difficult to enjoy conversations because it sounded like constant in-ear tinnitus.

The biggest disappointment, however, was the food. I’m not sure whether some reviewers are being served a different standard of food or whether expectations have simply been exaggerated, but our experience was far from what was advertised. The food was genuinely disappointing.

The Chicken Checkmate was not served with vegetables as described on the menu. Instead of steamed broccoli, it came with a small and unusual portion of salad. The Basrah Roll, which was supposed to contain juicy crab meat, appeared to use inexpensive seafood sticks instead and did not taste good. The Beef Steak Roll was served raw, which in itself is not an issue, but the beef was already starting to discolour, suggesting it had been cut and left sitting for some time. After one bite, it had an unpleasant sour taste.

The Beefed Up dish should have been one of the simplest dishes to execute, but again the beef was already drying out and lacked flavour. Even the sushi sauce was just plain soy sauce. For a restaurant focused on sushi, it was disappointing that a simple sauce combination of soy sauce, mirin, and rice vinegar wasn’t prepared.

Another issue was the quality of the ingredients and the value for money. The wasabi appeared to be made from powder rather than freshly prepared, which was disappointing considering the price point.

For the cost of the dishes, many items felt like they were made using cheaper alternatives, and several descriptions on the menu did not match what was actually served. The Basrah Roll, for example, was described as containing crab meat but appeared to use seafood sticks instead.

The sushi rolls also did not contain the fresh mango described in the menu. Instead, there seemed to only be a mango-style drizzle on top, which is very different from having mango as an ingredient inside the roll. This added to the feeling that the food was being presented differently from what was advertised.

Service was another major issue. The food took a long time to arrive, and the servers were not attentive. Nobody came over to check how we were finding the meal — I had to actively try to get their attention.

Considering we drove nearly 80 minutes to visit this restaurant, it was a huge waste of time, money, and effort.

Overall, this was one of the most disappointing restaurant experiences I’ve had. The expectations were high, but the food and service fell far below them, leaving a very negative impression.

Could never recommend and would advise against taking your car here for any work!

Buying from Trent Valley Windows has been a multi-year nightmare. The contract was signed in October 2023, and the entire project was riddled with gross incompetence.

1. Shocking Project Management: The installation took over six months instead of the estimated timeline. Work was cancelled at the very last minute on multiple occasions, disrupting our holidays.

2. Incompetent Design & Mistakes: The designer recommended seven spotlights, but during installation the electrician revealed that the design was physically impossible. We were forced to accept a compromised five-spotlight layout under significant stress simply to avoid further delays. Although the company previously offered a £400 goodwill payment for this issue, the after-sales service turned out to be far worse.

3. A Two-Year Battle for the Building Regulations Certificate: The contract included obtaining the Building Regulations Final Certificate, yet it took over two years after completion before we finally received it. During that time we repeatedly chased both Trent Valley Windows and its parent company, CO Home Improvements.

Only after we escalated the matter to the GGF did we finally receive the certificate. Although CO Home Improvements informed the GGF that the certificate had been issued directly to us on 15 June, we never received it from them. The certificate was eventually forwarded to us by the GGF following its intervention.

The certificate has now finally been resolved, but only after nearly three years of delays, repeated chasing, poor communication and unnecessary stress. I would strongly encourage anyone considering Trent Valley Windows to think very carefully before signing a contract.

one_star_reviews.text:
I rented a room in a shared property that was managed by Reed Residential from March 2025 until May 2026. Unfortunately, my experience was consistently poor and caused significant stress throughout my tenancy.

One of the most concerning issues was staff entering the property and tenants’ rooms without proper notice. On multiple occasions, rooms were accessed unexpectedly, including incidents where housemates were walked in on while in their rooms. Maintenance staff also entered my room using a spare key while I was absent, leaving the room in a mess and unplugging appliances, including my mini fridge, which resulted in water leaking onto the floor. When I raised concerns about this, the response I received was unprofessional and dismissive.

Communication was a recurring problem. Meetings were arranged and then cancelled without being rescheduled, emails often went unanswered, and different members of staff appeared unaware of previous conversations or agreements.

The property itself suffered from numerous maintenance issues, including problems with the shower, hob, windows, furniture, and mould. In several cases, intervention from the local council was required before repairs were carried out. The mould issue in my room was only addressed after council involvement.

My tenancy agreement included bills and communal cleaning. However, after Reed Residential took over management, the communal cleaning service largely stopped. Utilities also became problematic. I received correspondence from British Gas stating I was liable for bills despite my tenancy agreement confirming that bills were included. I also experienced internet outages, and when I contacted the provider, I was informed that payments had been outstanding.

The handling of my deposit at the end of the tenancy was particularly frustrating. I followed all instructions regarding check-out, cleaned my room thoroughly, and was initially told my deposit would be returned within seven days. This deadline repeatedly changed, communication became inconsistent, and I was eventually informed they could not access my room despite previously stating that an inspection had already been completed. It took numerous emails and the threat of formal action before my deposit was finally returned.

There were also issues regarding parking permits. My tenancy agreement entitled me to a free permit, but after Reed Residential took over, attempts were made to charge for permits. The car park was frequently overcrowded, with maintenance vehicles and stored items taking up spaces, making parking difficult even for permit holders.

Even after moving out, the communication issues continued. I recently received an email stating that I had an outstanding balance of over £600 for a period covering my move-out date and the following month. The email included a payment statement showing my previous payments and the alleged outstanding balance, making it appear to be a legitimate debt. Concerned by this, I contacted senior members of the team, who later confirmed and apologised that the email had been sent in error. While I appreciate the apology, receiving an incorrect demand for a substantial sum of money was unnecessarily stressful and could have been avoided had the relevant staff checked the information with colleagues before sending it.

Overall, I found Reed Residential’s management to be disorganised, unprofessional, and unresponsive. The lack of communication, repeated maintenance issues, concerns over property access, and difficulties recovering my deposit made this a very disappointing experience. I would strongly encourage prospective tenants, particularly students, to carefully consider these issues before renting through Reed Residential.

I visited this bike shop for the first time based on all the gleaming 5 star reviews. I supplied my rear wheel and sprocket carrier loose off the bike plus 3 bearings and 2 seals to have them installed.
When I picked up the wheel the internal sprocket carrier spacer was installed into the outside of the bearing not the inside. I was asked to bring it back the following week for them to rectify.
I took the wheel home and although awkward rectified this myself.
On inspection there was indentation damage to the rear faces of all 6 sprocket lugs. One so badly indented that the sprocket bolt would not go into the hole, I also rectified this myself.
The last item was the bearing which had not been fully pressed home into the carrier. There was a 1.5mm gap between the bearing and the face of the housing. This item meant that the sprocket carrier would not seat correctly in the hub.
Had the wheel been installed on the bike with this fault at the very least it would have meant the bearing failing prematurely and at worst the bearing seizing and possible catastrophic loss of control of the motorcycle.
If this had been an exam the person carrying out this work would have failed the test.

Upon re picking the car up he told us that the smoke was excess oil and that it would stop in a day or two. Half way home the car starts smokeing again with lights on the dash. I contacted adam and toom it straight back to him, they gave us a courtesy car which had worn bushes.

The following day it starts smoking again. I let adam know again that there was still an issue.
We then had to pay for a private inspection to be done. The inspection found that the vehicle had a coolent leek from the bottom hose due to a broken clip.

I started dealing with Tanya Kilmartin at Morris Solicitors following an accident in January 2023.

The other side admitted liability within a relatively short period of time, yet the progress of my case was extremely slow. It took around a year before I was seen by a medical expert, and throughout the case I often felt that I had to chase matters myself rather than being kept informed and updated.

One of the main issues was obtaining the interim payment. Rather than this being actively progressed, I found myself repeatedly having to pursue Tanya to get any movement on the matter.

The most concerning aspect arose when I was told that court proceedings had been issued so that a judge could determine whether I was entitled to further compensation. After being informed that proceedings had been issued, I heard nothing for months. Whenever I contacted Tanya for an update, I was repeatedly told that she was chasing the matter and pressing for progress.

Eventually, after becoming frustrated with the delays, I complained and dealt with John Morrison instead, as I no longer felt confident that the case was being progressed appropriately.

After I began dealing with John, it became apparent to me that court proceedings had not in fact been issued. Had proceedings been issued, I would have expected to receive a notice of hearing and any other relevant documentation, and I would have had to sign the necessary paperwork. Despite being told on numerous occasions that the matter was being pursued and chased, no such progress had been made. After dealing with John within a very short time court proceedings were progressed.

What should have been a straightforward case, given that liability was admitted early on, has only been finalised today despite the accident occurring in January 2023. In my view, the excessive delays, lack of progress, and the information I was given regarding court proceedings caused unnecessary stress and frustration throughout the claim.
When I was eventually awarded an interim payment, I was told that the funds would be received within 21 days. After the 23rd day had passed, I contacted the firm for an update and was informed that it would be chased.

I then contacted the firm again and was once more told that the payment would be chased and I would be contacted. However, after a few more days, when I made further enquiries, I was informed that the payment had already arrived.

This left me feeling frustrated and concerned about the communication surrounding the payment. In my view, there appeared to be unnecessary delays in providing me with accurate information, and I was left with the impression that matters were being stalled. I also felt that the payment may have been received earlier than I had been told.

I am sharing my experience so that others dealing with Tanya Kilmartin can make their own informed decisions, ask questions, and closely monitor the progress of their case. If you find yourself experiencing similar delays or communication issues, you may wish to consider requesting that another solicitor handle your matter.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was in two minds about writing this because I know how stretched our healthcare system is, and I have a great deal of respect for the people who work within it. However, I cannot stop thinking about the care I received during one of the most difficult periods of my life.

After almost a week of relentless urinary urgency and frequency, nausea, sleepless nights, and overwhelming anxiety and stress, I drove myself to this urgent care centre hoping for reassurance, advice, or simply some compassion.

Despite being the only patient waiting to be seen for an illness-related issue, I waited for over two hours before I was finally called in to see the nurse on duty.

I explained everything I had been experiencing, how much I was struggling, and how desperately I needed some guidance. I appreciate that there may have been very little that could be done medically at that stage. What I did not expect was the complete lack of empathy.

I was told there was essentially “nothing I can do for you” and advised to go home and “stock up on adult diapers and pads” because this could be “your life from now on - diapers and suffering.” I was also told I needed to see a specialist, but that the waiting list was long because “they’re free of charge, so they do what they want.”

The words themselves were upsetting, but it was the manner in which they were delivered that has stayed with me. I felt dismissed, as though my distress and suffering were an inconvenience rather than something worthy of compassion. By the end of the consultation, the nurse appeared frustrated that I had come seeking help at all.

I left without any meaningful advice, reassurance, or support. More than anything, I left feeling abandoned and completely alone at a time when I was already at my lowest.

I fully understand the immense pressures facing our healthcare staff, and this review is not a criticism of the system itself. It is about the importance of kindness. Even when there is little that can be done medically, patients deserve to be listened to, treated with dignity, and shown compassion. A few empathetic words can make an enormous difference to someone who is frightened and vulnerable. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

Even after my daughter sat on it and it appeared to fit her well, he continued to argue rather than assist.

When I said I would take the bike, he responded rudely, saying I could not just take it and ride it on the road, and repeatedly challenged what I meant, even after I clarified that I meant I wanted to order it. He then said delivery would only be available on Tuesday, which I accepted, but instead of helping me complete the purchase, he called another branch and told me to go there instead.

He also mentioned a £10 assembly charge. I simply asked whether it was possible to buy the displayed bike, as I had previously done this when buying a bike for my son from Halfords. Instead of answering professionally, he spoke to his colleague on the phone in a mocking way, saying that “they don’t understand what assembling the bike means for £10”. I fully understand that ordering may take time and that assembly charges may apply. I explained that the NHS usually starts treating without a diagnosis, and that I've been told by NHS staff that they don't think diagnosis is helpful. And that I'm a childhood and early adulthood survivor of medical neglect (hit for health problems instead of taken to a doctor, and disallowed from leaving my home so unable to secret visit a doctor) and that sometimes mental health problems themselves can make it harder to get through administrative processes or attend appointments. I asked if there a part of the form for mental health issues in general that aren't diagnosed, but she said there isn't.

So, an organisation in "social services" has a policy that they know is incompatible with the main healthcare system in the UK.

One star is far too many for the experiences I’ve had with vets4pets Somercotes.  Genuinely one of the most insensitive experiences I have ever had from a vet practice.

My fur baby, Bayleigh, had been under their care for ongoing health issues and I informed them immediately after she passed away at home with the help of an out of hours vets who I can’t thank enough for their help and compassion. You would think that would be enough to stop appointment reminders being sent. Apparently not.

Since her death, I have continued receiving multiple reminders for blood tests and follow-up appointments despite being told their “system had been updated.”

Losing a pet is heartbreaking enough without having to repeatedly reopen the wound every time another text or reminder comes through. If anyone should understand the emotional impact of losing an animal, it should be a veterinary clinic, yet the complete lack of care, attention and compassion shown here has been shocking.

What makes this even worse is that Bayleigh actually received her end-of-life care through a different vet because I wanted her to pass peacefully at home surrounded by family. One single interaction with that vet during the worst moment of my life showed me more compassion, empathy and humanity than I experienced in nearly 10 years bringing my dogs here.

Mistakes happen once. Continuing to send reminders after being notified of a death is just careless and deeply insensitive.

Safe to say I will now be moving my remaining boys to another vet because this experience completely destroyed any trust I had in the practice. Compassion costs absolutely nothing.

If you've ever wondered what "deep cleaned" means in estate agent language, it apparently translates to "bring your own mop and an entire day of your life." When we moved in, the place was so filthy that even the cleaning products looked like they wanted to move out. We spent a full day scrubbing it before moving our stuff in.

The fun didn't stop there. Before we agreed to rent, we were told the property was £950 a month. Once we said we wanted it, the price suddenly became £1,100. By that point we had already invested time and effort, so we reluctantly accepted. It felt like a classic bait and switch.

The boiler was broken from day one, in February, and when they finally sent an engineer, the agent acted as though he had performed an act of great heroism. All we wanted was a property that could produce heat, which seems like a reasonable expectation for £1,100 a month.

We reported broken fence panels around 18 months prior to moving out, and those panels were still out there bravely clinging to life on the day we left. I think at this point they have become part of the local ecosystem.

And to top it off, despite the EPC stating there was loft insulation, there was absolutely none. I can only assume it was imaginary insulation, very energy efficient in theory, less so in practice.

Four months after moving out, we were still receiving viewing notices for the property. We can only assume we remained "current tenants" in their system, which makes sense, updating a spreadsheet presumably falls under the same priority bracket as fixing fence panels.

If you're a tenant who wants an honest and dependable estate agent, or a landlord who's looking for an agent who actually looks after your investment, don't choose Comfort Properties.

Inconsistent, Confrontational and Exhausting — I've Finally Given Up!!

After numerous frustrating visits to Boots pharmacy on Lower Parliament Street in Nottingham, I've reached the point where I simply won't return!!

The problems are consistent and repeated: long queues, an unpredictable experience and a staff approach that too often feels more like an interrogation than a pharmacy visit. I want to be clear — I have no issue with pharmacists carrying out proper safety checks. That is their professional duty and I respect it. What I object to is the way those checks are sometimes conducted and the alarming lack of consistency between staff members.

The experience varies dramatically depending on who is serving. Some staff are professional, efficient and genuinely helpful. Others make customers feel like they're under suspicion for attempting to buy routine over-the-counter medication. There is no apparent standard being applied consistently across the team.

My most recent visit was the final straw. I came in with an obvious, painful eye infection — visible redness, clear symptoms and asked for chloramphenicol eye drops. Despite explaining everything clearly, I felt challenged and doubted at every turn. I was almost told off for having used lubricating eye drops beforehand to ease my discomfort while waiting to access treatment!! That was the moment I decided enough was enough. This wasn't an isolated incident.

On a previous occasion I was refused products I have routinely purchased together at other pharmacies without any difficulty. The decisions seem to rest entirely on the individual serving you rather than any consistent professional standard — which leaves customers confused, frustrated and frankly wondering what they can rely on.

There is a real difference between safeguarding and making customers feel like a problem to be managed. Boots has consistently failed to strike that balance at this branch. I now use Glasshouse Pharmacy and the contrast is stark. The service is efficient, the staff are helpful and consistent and I leave feeling supported rather than scrutinised. It is everything a pharmacy visit should be.

Boots would do well to look seriously at the customer experience at this branch — the queues, the inconsistency and the unnecessarily confrontational approach are driving loyal customers away. In my case, permanently!!

I wanted to provide feedback regarding my recent experience purchasing a vehicle from Toyota Group 1 Nottingham.

Unfortunately, my experience has been disappointing from start to finish and has fallen significantly below the level of customer service I expected from a Toyota dealership.

The main issue throughout the process has been a lack of communication. Telephone calls frequently went unanswered, and on several occasions I was promised a call back that never came. As a customer, I found myself constantly having to chase for updates rather than being kept informed about the progress of my purchase.

I was also disappointed that my vehicle was not delivered on the agreed and booked delivery date. I had arranged my work commitments around the delivery and consequently lost a day's earnings waiting for a vehicle that never arrived. While delays can sometimes happen, the lack of communication surrounding the situation made the experience even more frustrating.

In addition, I have since discovered that the vehicle has still not been transferred through the DVLA into the name of the new registered keeper. This is something I would have expected to be completed as part of the normal sales process and has only added to my concerns regarding the administration and attention to detail involved in my purchase.

I also remain concerned that not all Toyota Approved Used checks and preparations appear to have been completed as expected. The Toyota Approved Used programme was an important factor in my decision to purchase the vehicle, and I expected the standards associated with that programme to be fully met.

Even now, communication remains poor. I am still waiting for a proper introduction and handover of the vehicle, including guidance on its features and systems. This is something I would normally expect as part of the customer experience when purchasing a vehicle from a main dealer.

The issues mentioned above represent only some of the problems I have experienced. There have been numerous other examples of poor follow-up, broken promises, and a general lack of customer care throughout the process.

Overall, I feel let down by the service I have received from Toyota Group 1 Nottingham. Purchasing a vehicle should be an exciting and positive experience, but unfortunately this has been overshadowed by poor communication, administrative issues, and a lack of attention to the customer experience.

I hope this feedback is taken constructively and used to improve the experience for future customers. At present, based on my own experience, I would find it difficult to recommend Toyota Group 1 Nottingham to friends, family, or colleagues.

one_star_reviews.text:
Outdated model with excessive fees and poor value

I would not recommend St James’s Place.

My experience/opinion is that the whole model feels outdated: high charges, restricted advice, expensive funds, and performance that does not seem to justify the cost. When you compare it with a simple low-cost global tracker, the value proposition looks extremely weak.

What concerns me most is the historic fee structure. SJP has been criticised for things like high ongoing charges and early exit fees, which in my view made it harder for clients to leave once they realised they were not getting good value. That kind of model feels very old-fashioned and not aligned with what modern investors should expect.

The fees are not just slightly high. They can be astronomically high compared with low-cost alternatives, and that matters because every extra percentage point in fees compounds against the client over time. You can end up paying a premium price while still getting underwhelming performance.

To me, SJP seems to benefit from the fact that many clients do not know how cheap and simple investing can be elsewhere. Once you understand the alternatives, it is very difficult to justify paying so much for restricted advice and expensive managed funds.

In my view, this is an antiquated, poor-value wealth management model that relies far too much on complexity, trust, and client ignorance rather than genuinely superior outcomes.

one_star_reviews.text:
I purchased a used MG HS from MG Sandicliffe on 26/05, and it was delivered on 29/05. Unfortunately, my experience with the dealership has been disappointing from the very beginning.

The first issue arose before delivery when I was sent a vehicle order and invoice showing a price approximately £500 higher than the price advertised on AutoTrader. I was told the dealership's system showed a different price, and I was then asked to provide a screenshot of the advertised price myself. I found this to be very unprofessional, particularly as the error originated from the dealership.

When the car was delivered, I discovered it was covered in scratches that had not been disclosed prior to the sale. I appreciate that a used vehicle will have some age-related marks, but the vehicle had been described as "clean inside and out", and I specifically requested a live video walkaround before purchasing. Instead, I was sent a low-quality video that did not accurately show the condition of the vehicle’s bodywork.

During further inspection, I also discovered that the tow eye cover was missing and a small dent on the driver’s door. These issues had not been disclosed prior to the sale.

The explanation I was given for the scratches was that the car was black and dirty, so they had not noticed them. I was also told they had not noticed the missing tow eye cover or the dent on the driver’s door. This raises concerns about how thoroughly the vehicle was inspected before being offered for sale.

Since then, I have contacted both the salesperson and the sales manager on numerous occasions. I obtained several repair quotations, including a very reasonable quote of £480, yet the only offer made was £50 towards polishing the scratches, which would not rectify the damage. Since then, my emails have largely gone unanswered, and I have received repeated promises over the phone without any meaningful resolution.

My experience with Shaf was equally disappointing. Communication was prompt while the sale was being completed, but once issues with the vehicle were raised, communication became poor and responses were inconsistent. Rather than taking ownership of the problems, I felt I was met with excuses instead of solutions. Overall, I felt there was a lack of accountability and professionalism when dealing with my concerns, and the after-sales service fell well below the standard I expected.

I am now escalating this matter through the appropriate complaints process and will be referring it to the Motor Ombudsman. I am also considering further action through the small claims court if the matter remains unresolved.

My advice to anyone considering buying a used vehicle from this dealership is to inspect it thoroughly in person before committing to the purchase. If you are buying remotely, insist on a high-quality live video inspection and do not rely solely on the description provided. In my experience, once the sale was completed, resolving issues became extremely difficult.

Overall, this has been a stressful and disappointing experience at a time when I urgently needed a replacement vehicle. I placed my trust in MG Sandicliffe to provide a vehicle that matched its description, and unfortunately that trust was not rewarded.

On 13 May 2026, I attended an appointment for my dog’s skin condition. Following the consultation, I was advised that the total cost of treatment would be £288.89.

At reception, I informed staff that I had pet insurance. I was asked to provide my insurance provider details and policy number, which I did. I was then informed that I only needed to pay the £90 excess, which I paid immediately. The receptionist clearly stated that no further action was required from me and that, if there were any issues with the insurance claim or if it was rejected, the practice would contact me within five days.

I received no communication from the practice regarding any problems with the claim. As a result, I reasonably believed that the insurance process had been completed successfully.

However, on 8 June 2026 at 6:06 a.m., I received an email stating that I owed an outstanding balance of £198.89. Concerned by this, I contacted the practice at 9:03 a.m. to understand why I had received this demand for payment.

During the call, I was informed that the practice had allegedly attempted to contact me on multiple occasions to advise that I needed to complete additional paperwork. This is incorrect. I did not receive any phone calls, emails, text messages, or voicemails regarding this matter.

The only contact I received from the practice was on 1 June 2026 regarding my dog’s test results. During my call on 8 June, I was told there was a different telephone number recorded on my file. This explanation raises further concerns, as the practice was clearly able to contact me regarding my dog’s test results on 1 June. If my contact details were incorrect, I do not understand how communication was successful on that occasion but not regarding the insurance claim.

I would also like to highlight a further communication failure. On 1 June 2026, Bruna Kremer attempted to contact me by telephone. Unfortunately, I missed this call due to being at work. Upon receiving the email containing my dog’s test results, I telephoned the practice the following day at approximately 5:12 p.m. and requested to speak with Bruna Kremer. I was advised by the receptionist that she would arrange for Bruna Kremer to contact me the following day.

No call was received. I did not receive any further communication by telephone, email, or text message regarding my dog’s care or the insurance claim.

I am extremely disappointed by the lack of communication and the way this matter has been handled. I have been a client of Springfield Veterinary Group since 2020 and previously attended the White Lane branch, where I never experienced any issues of this nature.

The failures in communication from the Wickersley branch have caused me significant and unnecessary stress. I am currently six months pregnant, and receiving an unexpected demand for nearly £200, after being assured that no further action was required from me, has caused considerable anxiety and upset.

I would give zero stars if I could. The experience at this branch has been extremely disappointing, and as a result, my dog and I will be moving to a different veterinary practice. I can no longer recommend this branch based on the service we received.

After months of progressing our purchase, Persimmon/Charles Church pulled the sale just one week before exchange. The experience has completely destroyed any trust I had in Persimmon/Charles Church. Charles Church treated my young family appallingly after seven months of watching our new home be built.

We reserved plot 57 at Hallows Rise last year on a part exchange with everything agreed.

We watched it be built and went back and forth every few weeks to view the property at each stage which was very exciting.

We paid for 35k of extras to be fitted and the house looked beautiful for myself, my wife and three children, till the nightmare began.

On the day we were expecting to sign our two weeks notice paperwork to move, we were asked to go to the office. Lyam who was brilliant from the sales team was joined by another manager.

They proceeded to deliver news that they could no longer do a part exchange on our current property because of rights for access to our road, which was just nonsense as we were covered by insurances and everything we needed.

They said they would do it but only if we took 30k less for our house. They claimed it was a conversation ongoing for months but our solicitors knew nothing about it.

We offered 10k which was refused and then decided to meet their expectations of 30k but asked to complete paperwork that week due to a busy June schedule.

They moved the goalposts again and said they couldn’t do the 30k any longer, but would hold our property for three months for us to sell privately and would give our extras included free of charge if we did sell.

We spoke as a family and then found a way to buy the house without the need to sell our home first and we would sell later. We had the cash and could meet all the terms and said we wanted confirmation the 35k extras were still included as our stamp duty would be higher.

The sales director ignored calls, i rang the regional MD Gareth Hankin who’s number i was given and explained our situation, he said he’d be happy to help but was clearly annoyed we had his number, kept asking and asking.

I emailed sales director Tom Baskett and said we have cash with solicitors letter confirming proof of funds etc, we are ready to move but can we get it over the line, he said “yes let’s have a call tomorrow between 2-4pm”.

We went to the office for 3pm as we’d requested. Tom was a no show, he ignored his sales teams calls.

4pm email from solicitors saying never ring the MD again calling my one phone call was apparently harassment, and claiming we’d said we had his home address, couldn’t be more of a lie.

18:30pm an email saying they were no longer selling us the house. Our solicitors said they’d told them they didn’t have to give a reason or justify themselves. They even told our mortgage advisory we had tried to change deposit amounts.

It’s disgusting an MD’s ego had made them pull out or that they regretted offering us the extras for free. Cutting their nose off to spite their face.

Our daughter was in the showroom crying her eyes out and the sales director midway through the process with the 30k reduction of offer had tried to throw his upset sales team under the bus claiming they know.

These are families Persimmon are dealing with and they have no empathy. It’s vile and regulations should be better to stop this from happening.

I’d give 0 stars if I could and recommend avoiding Persimmon and Charles Church at all costs.

Today, after picking up my children from school, we went shopping at Tesco. At the entrance, there was a lady (around 50–55 years old, short hair, glasses) handing out free food samples. Unfortunately, I didn’t catch her name.

I stopped because I was interested in trying a mozzarella sample with some herbs on top. I took one, tasted it, and asked her what it was because I really liked it. Before she could answer, my 5-year-old son reached for a sample as well. She immediately stopped him, took it out of his hand, and said very seriously, “Don’t touch, just one.”

I assume she meant that I had already taken one, but the way she spoke to my child was unnecessary and upsetting. My son looked confused and disappointed because he simply wanted to taste what his mum had just tried. After noticing my reaction, she offered my son and my daughter a piece of ham instead. Then she looked at my son and said, “You say thank you.”

At that moment, I felt very uncomfortable. I wanted to speak to the manager, but my husband, who had been looking at something else nearby, asked me to let it go when I explained what had happened.

I don’t know whether she simply doesn’t like children or whether there was another reason for her behaviour. My children were speaking Romanian with me, and I can’t say why she reacted the way she did. What I do know is that it left my little boy embarrassed, looking down at the floor because he wasn’t allowed to try the same free sample that I had just tasted.

If I had known this was how we would be treated, I would never have stopped. It is a shame that a 5-year-old child was made to feel this way over a free sample.

During the appointment, I questioned the colour as it looked too pale, but the technician said he couldn’t challenge the decision. In the end, the result was completely off from what I asked for.

I wasn’t happy with the outcome and insisted the nails needed to be changed. My daughter supported me in this, as I don’t think the owner would have agreed otherwise. Eventually, she did agree to have them redone.

I wish I had kept the photos of the original colours, because the colours were so off and looked horribly wrong and mismatched for a French tip. Even after they were redone, they were better, but still not perfect.

When the nails were redone by the same technician, she repeatedly said it was “the first and last time” she would do this, which felt guilt-inducing and inappropriate. When I offered to tip the technician, she implied I should be paying her instead due to the cost of redoing them.

She refused to accept my Blue Light Card, saying it had already cost her a lot to redo my nails. I felt I was being penalised for a mistake that wasn’t mine, which I found unprofessional and poor customer service.

The vets here misdiagnosed my guinea pig due to incompetence and a lack of proper investigation. We were told that she had an terminal bladder tumour and to just make her comfortable as there was nothing to be done. After a week, I felt that this was not right and took her to another vet. He carried out proper testing and diagnosed her with an ovarian tumour that should have be removable. However, due to her lack of timely diagnosis, she had deteriorated too quickly and did not survive the surgery. I have since consulted a third independent vet who informed me that the method used (an ultrasound) by Pets4Vets to diagnose her with a bladder tumour would not even have been able to do so. I attempted to receive some kind of apology or compensation repeatedly, even going through citizens advice to reach an agreement. However, Pets4Vets refused all mediation and stated that they supported the diagnosis despite another vet carrying out a surgery that literally definitively contradicts this. I am devastated by my loss and felt so poorly and insensitively treated by the vets here. I understand that mistakes happen, but an apology and admittance of an incorrect diagnosis would have gone a long way. Please do not bring your exotic animals here as the 'exotic animal' specialist was not equipped to treat my guinea pig.
