I’ve been with this surgery since I was born. First in Evington, and now it’s moved to netherhall. Dr Wood was absolutely brilliant before. In Evington, I actively avoided Dr Toby Cheesman, because of what felt like a lack of regard of my problems. After suffering from cystic painful acne from the age of 10, I went every so often asking Dr Cheesman for help with it, complaining about it. It wasn’t until the age of 15 when I finally addressed it to Dr Wood where he immediately referred me to dermatology. My dermatologist was absolutely shocked at the time for how it had gotten so bad until I was referred. But I decided to just brush it under the carpet, and not say anything about it, doctors aren’t going to get it right 100% of the time, I would’ve liked a referral a long time before, but it’s okay, nobody’s perfect, it would be absurd to expect perfection. Since then, I’ve seen Dr Cheesman reluctantly a few times and never really felt heard by him, but to be honest, this review isn’t about him, because to a degree, it does actually look like he tries to be a good doctor. So he’s clearly making an effort. My review is really about Dr M Harrison.

I’m not the type of person to go to the GP. I avoid going most of the time because most things will eventually pass so I just don’t see the need to go. But when I do go, it’s only when I know and feel that something is really wrong, or it’s been going on for too long now and getting worse.

I saw Dr Harrison recently, and she had a horrible patient/bedside manner. She genuinely said to me that I’m taking up too much time, and now I’m making her late. Bear in mind, my appt was for x am, she brought me in at x:05, and she told me this at x:12. I hadn’t even been there for a full 10 minutes! Zero regard for how she’s making the patient feel, zero respect for the patient’s time, zero effort to build a rapport and understand what’s going on. I understand that this is a job. I understand that you have a full clinic. I understand that you have many patients to see. But, I hadn’t even been there for my full allotted time of 10 minutes. And please, you got into this profession to help people. You’re in a role to care for people. I ask you to please renew your intentions. I can appreciate that doctors are being overworked and underpaid, but please stop taking it out on your patients and just take it up with management instead. Genuinely cried after my appointment. Before she insinuated to me that she essentially wants me to get out so she can be done w the appt, I had told her that I had been struggling recently, and she just brushed past it. I’m just appalled at the lack of care in this visit.

​I bought a used BMW from this dealership that turned out to be completely defective and unroadworthy from day one. Within the first 3 days, a heavy vibration was reported and a fractured suspension coil spring was diagnosed by their own mechanic, but repairs were constantly delayed and stalled with excuses. The car also had water leaking into the rear footwell.
​During a necessary trip, I was forced to pay out of pocket to replace dangerous, dry-rotted tyres that were splitting. On day 28, the car suffered a catastrophic prop-shaft/rear diff failure (the exact area causing the original vibration) and became completely immobile, this fault was well known as well. On the day it broke down, the brakes were also smoking directly into the cabin and oil leak behind engine and top of gearbox.
​When I legally rejected the vehicle within the 30-day window, the dealer refused a full refund and tried to unlawfully deduct nearly £1,000 for mileage (1,866 miles). To avoid a lengthy Small Claims Court battle, I had to accept a financial loss just to get my money back and end the nightmare.
​Shockingly, the dealer has now put the exact same car straight back up for sale at the original price, using the same old MOT, without legally verifying that these major safety issues have been properly resolved.
​Terrible vehicle, shocking communication, and zero respect for consumer rights. Avoid this dealership at all costs or at the very least, avoid this specific car!

If you value your sanity, your personal data, or basic human communication, I’d recommend avoiding this company like it’s offering free hugs during a zombie apocalypse.

From start to finish, the entire process was an Olympic-level disaster. Calling my case handler? Impossible. Requesting callbacks? Apparently just a fun decorative feature on their website. Emails? Oh, they do reply… eventually… usually after you’ve sent enough follow-ups to qualify as a part-time stalker.

My case handler, Halima, seemed deeply committed to the exciting corporate philosophy of “ignore the client until they lose the will to live.” To be fair though, this appeared to be less of an individual talent and more of a company-wide mission statement.

As a first-time buyer, I was absolutely thrilled when my purchase was delayed by SIX MONTHS — so close to collapse that the seller nearly walked away. Nothing says “welcome to homeownership” quite like constant stress and the very real possibility of becoming homeless before you even get the keys.

But wait, there’s more.

During the process, they accidentally sent my bank statements and passport copies to a third party. Did they notify me? Of course not. The THIRD PARTY had to tell me. To this day, I have no idea who else may now have my personal information floating around like confetti at a data breach parade.

Then, months after completion, the managing company contacted me about unpaid service charges from before I even owned the property. Apparently checking outstanding balances was simply too ambitious a task. So naturally, I got stuck paying someone else’s debt. Love that for me.

And finally — because every comedy needs a grand finale — a few months ago they mailed me TWO original marriage certificates belonging to complete strangers. Spoiler alert: I’m not married. I emailed them to let them know about their mistake, partly because I’m a decent human being and partly because I assume those people may someday want to legally separate. Unsurprisingly, I never received a response.

Ironically, their response to this review was the quickest I’ve ever heard back from them. Sadly, instead of replying to the actual email I sent warning them they had mailed me marriage certificates belonging to complete strangers, they simply informed me that my case was “from 2024” and that they’ve “improved their service since then.”

Bold strategy.

Especially considering I’ve attached a photo of the certified letter THEY sent me in FEBRUARY 2026 containing said random strangers’ marriage certificates. Nothing screams “we’ve improved” quite like continuing to breach client confidentiality years later with the enthusiasm of a company running a data leak loyalty scheme.

At this point, I’m honestly just waiting for them to accidentally send me someone’s kidney transplant paperwork and a Tesco Clubcard application.

I have been getting intimate waxes regularly for around four years and have never experienced anything like this before.

Jasmine was pleasant enough, but I felt that the appointment was rushed. During the wax she was very aggressive, particularly in my intimate area, and didn’t check in to see if I was okay despite how painful it was. I understand waxing can be uncomfortable, but this was far more painful than any wax I’ve had previously.

When I left the salon, the area was extremely red and sore. Two weeks later, I developed painful bumps that became much worse. The discomfort became so severe that I had to see my doctor, who diagnosed an infection and prescribed antibiotics.

I’ve always left previous waxing appointments with smooth results, so this experience was very disappointing. Unfortunately, instead of the usual outcome, I’ve been left dealing with painful bumps, soreness, and an infection.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously, as clients should feel cared for during such a sensitive treatment. I would encourage the salon to ensure therapists regularly check on clients’ comfort throughout the appointment and avoid rushing treatments.

Extremely disappointing and unprofessional experience for viewing “3 Lupin Close, Edwalton, Nottingham, NG12 4HU” on Saturday June 27th 2026

I had a viewing appointment booked for 2:45 pm, so I left home on time. Due to unexpected traffic, I realised I might be 5–10 minutes late. At around 2:40 pm, I called the Holden Copley office to inform them that I would arrive between 2:50 pm and 2:55 pm. I was assured that this was absolutely fine, that the team would be informed, and I was advised to continue to the property.

I arrived at 2:55 pm, rang the doorbell, and waited outside for around five minutes, assuming someone might still be inside. When nobody answered, I called the office again, only to be told that the sales executive had already left after waiting just two minutes, until approximately 2:47 pm, because his diary was “very busy.”

What makes this even more frustrating is the complete double standard. Only last week, when viewing another one of their property (14 Autumn Close, West Bridgford, Nottingham, NG2 7YL, on Monday 22nd June), their own sales executive arrived 15 minutes late. On that occasion, I patiently waited outside in the hot afternoon sun with my 5 and 8-year-old children, and I even had to cancel an important office meeting because of their delay. I accepted it without complaint because I understood that delays can happen.

However, yesterday when I informed them in advance that I would be delayed by no more than 10 minutes, they couldn’t extend the same basic courtesy. Instead, the appointment was effectively cancelled after waiting just two minutes, despite the office knowing exactly when I would arrive.

To make matters worse, when I requested that the sales executive return to the property, I was spoken to in a dismissive and rude manner. I was repeatedly told that his diary was “very busy” and that he would not be coming back. There was no apology, no attempt to resolve the situation, and no appreciation for the time I had spent travelling.

This is not how customers should be treated. If you expect clients to accommodate your delays, you should be willing to show the same flexibility when customers communicate honestly and courteously in advance. The lack of professionalism, poor communication, and complete disregard for customer time have left me extremely disappointed. Based on this experience, I would seriously question whether Holden Copley genuinely values its customers.

Poor experience overall.

While the sofa itself is nice, the overall experience with Fabb Furniture has been extremely disappointing due to poor service and misleading information.

At the point of sale, I was told the sofa would be delivered within around 6 weeks. In reality, it took 12 weeks to arrive, with little communication or transparency during the delay.

More concerning, I was explicitly sold a “lifetime guarantee” covering the frame and mechanical components with no call-out fees, which was a key reason I chose this retailer. However, when a fault developed (failed internal springs), I was then told I had to pay a £72 call-out fee just to have it inspected — completely contradicting what I was told when purchasing.

When I challenged this, Fabb refused to proceed with the repair or even continue communication unless I paid the fee. This is unacceptable and shows a complete lack of willingness to resolve a legitimate complaint.

Overall, this has been a frustrating experience involving delayed delivery, misleading sales information, and appalling customer service.

I would strongly advise getting everything in writing and being very cautious before buying from Fabb Furniture.

One of the most frustrating experiences I have had when buying a car.

I purchased a Ford Fiesta from this dealership expecting a reliable vehicle and some peace of mind from the warranty that came with it. Instead, the car broke down within the first two weeks of ownership and had to be recovered by the AA and taken back to my home. Having a newly purchased car fail so quickly was both stressful and extremely inconvenient.

Unfortunately, the problems did not stop there. The boot latch also developed a fault and needed replacing, leaving me to deal with yet another repair bill shortly after purchasing the vehicle. The unexpected costs quickly added up and placed unnecessary financial pressure on me.

The biggest disappointment was the way the warranty issues were handled. When I contacted the dealership regarding repairs that I believed should have been covered, I found the information provided to be unclear and inconsistent. Important details and limitations of the warranty were not properly explained at the point of sale, which left me with a completely different understanding of what was actually covered. As a result, I ended up paying for repairs that I reasonably expected the warranty to cover.

Good customer service is about supporting customers when problems arise, but I felt let down when I needed help the most. Instead of finding solutions, I was left feeling frustrated, out of pocket, and disappointed by the lack of transparency.

Buying a car should be an exciting experience, not one filled with breakdowns, repair costs, and disputes over warranty coverage. Based on my experience, I would not return to this dealership and cannot recommend it to others.

I am disappointed to see AST Assistance publicly state that they had “no record” of me as a client when I dealt directly with members of their team, including Mark, Davar, and Robyn, during the period from 2023 into 2025.

For clarity, this review relates to my direct experience as a paying client of AST Assistance in relation to a landlord possession/eviction matter. I communicated with the company primarily by email, alongside occasional telephone calls, received invoices and case correspondence from them, and was involved throughout the associated court process.

This review reflects my genuine personal experience with the company and the service provided.

Communication throughout the matter was, in my experience, inconsistent, unclear, and difficult to follow. Information was often vague, and despite repeated assurances that matters were progressing, meaningful updates or practical guidance were limited. There were also multiple occasions where information and documentation that had already been provided was requested again, which contributed to confusion and delays in progressing the matter.

One of my main concerns was the ongoing escalation of costs. The service initially appeared straightforward and reasonably priced; however, fees increased significantly as the matter progressed, often without corresponding clarity regarding outcomes, next steps, or overall strategy.

I also remain dissatisfied with the handling of paperwork and the overall management of the case. Documentation prepared during the process contained inconsistencies, unclear wording, and drafting issues that later became matters of concern during proceedings. In my view, aspects of the paperwork lacked clarity and appeared to complicate matters further rather than simplify them.

Although AST Assistance referred to the involvement of an external legal partner, my communications remained almost entirely with AST Assistance directly, and I never had meaningful direct communication with the legal representative involved. The documentation produced through that process contained inconsistencies and aspects of the wording and structure that I found difficult to interpret clearly.

Another concern was the extent to which I was repeatedly asked to prepare or rewrite substantial factual statements and information myself for inclusion within court documentation, despite engaging a company advertising specialist assistance in this area.

Overall, I found the service lacked the level of clarity, structure, and specialist guidance that had been expected at the outset. The process became time-consuming, stressful, and financially draining without achieving the outcome anticipated.

For completeness, my review reflects my genuine personal experience as a paying client of AST Assistance during the handling of my landlord possession matter. My comments are based on my direct interactions, correspondence, invoices, and documentation received throughout the process.

While I note the company’s position regarding the involvement of external solicitors, my communications and overall management experience remained primarily through AST Assistance and members of their team. My review relates to the quality, clarity, consistency, and handling of the service experience as I personally encountered it.

The fact that no formal complaint procedure was initiated at the time does not prevent a client from later providing feedback or sharing their experience through a review platform. Equally, previous correspondence stating that I was “not making a complaint” reflected the context of that communication at that specific time.

I stand by this review as an honest and factual account of my experience based on documented communications and correspondence relating to the matter.

Extremely poor, chaotic and stressful experience with E.ON Next.

This has been one of the most unnecessarily frustrating customer service experiences I have dealt with. What should have been a straightforward energy account has turned into a complete mess of confusing bills, estimated readings, unexplained balance changes, reversed charges, large payment demands and generic replies that do not properly answer the questions being asked.

We have spent an unreasonable amount of time trying to understand what E.ON Next has actually done with the account. Instead of receiving a clear, transparent breakdown, we have had to chase repeatedly, ask for escalation, request historic statements, ask for proper explanations and try to piece everything together ourselves. Customers should not have to act like forensic accountants just to understand their own energy bill.

The whole process has caused unnecessary stress, wasted valuable time and created huge anxiety. It is incredibly frustrating when a large company sends confusing billing information, demands large payments, and then fails to provide clear accountability when challenged.

The complaint handling has been especially disappointing. We asked for proper escalation, complaints manager details, clear procedures and a responsible person to deal with the matter. Instead, the replies have felt generic, incomplete and disorganised. At one point, correspondence was even addressed incorrectly, which is very concerning when the complaint itself is about account accuracy, billing confusion and poor internal handling.

This is not just bad customer service. It feels like a serious failure of basic account management, communication and accountability. When a customer raises a serious billing dispute, E.ON Next should provide a full audit trail, clear explanations, named responsibility and proper management oversight. Instead, we have had back and forth, vague responses, more questions, and no proper resolution.

The amount of unnecessary drama, time-wasting and stress this has caused is completely unacceptable. A company of this size should not be this disorganised. Customers should not have to fight for basic transparency, accurate billing and a proper complaints process.

Based on this experience, I would strongly advise anyone dealing with E.ON Next to keep every email, take regular meter photos, check every bill carefully, keep bank payment records, and put every complaint in writing. Do not rely on vague reassurances or phone calls without written confirmation.

Very disappointing. Very stressful. Very badly handled.

Upon first glance, 3 of the 4 wheels that had apparently been 'fully refurbished' all had curb damage. Popped the bonnet to check the engine and to my surprise, the bonnet struts had failed resulting in the the bonnet crashing down on my head. Reported this to the sales advisor immediately who suggested they would send someone to collect the car, driving it back to Nottingham and then back to me, a 200 mile round trip on a car I had only just purchased. The day after delivery, once the rain had stopped, I wiped the car down to check the paintwork to find laquer peel across the back bumper, this was also reported. After refusing the car to be driven back to Nottingham, they reluctantly agreed to recover it. This left me without the car I had just purchased for nearly a week and without transport. On return, the bonnet struts had been replaced, however the wheels had been poorly repaired and the paintwork which I expected to be resprayed, had simply been wet sanded and polished, leaving the outline of the peeled laquer still visible. After losing faith and reporting this to the dealer, a good will gesture was offered amd accepted. A week later, upon reviewing the service history, I discovered the differential service had been missed prior to sale and was out by approximately 7300 miles. This was raised as a formal complaint and once they accepted responsibility they once again attempted to send someone to collect the car and drive it back to nottingham. I repeated my comment from the first time this was suggested, especially since a high risk item like a differential certainly shouldnt be driven all the way back.  They offered to complete the service at my nearest branch, I opted to have it done at a specialist whilst also having the gearbox service done which was also needed. Group 1 then re-embursed the cost of the service.
Fast forward 2 months and the performance exhaust developed a rattle (a very common problem) bearing on mind I am still within the 6 months Consumer protection period, group 1 inspect the car and suggest that manufacturers guidance is to 'grease' the area. Anyone who knows about these cars knows this is a maintenance approach and not a permanent fix. I refused this point blank and then was ignored for long periods. Bearing in mind, the pre inspection report I received with the car stated the exhaust to be green (perfect working order).
Group 1 have now refused to replace the section of the exhaust which is the only guaranteed fix. To add insult to injury, they offered to buy back the car a at a usage per mile rate of £1.57!!!!! Official guidance is 25p to 45p per mile!!!! I have only covered 1200 miles in 5 months!!!! This is now in the hands of the Ombudsman. No doubt customer services will reply to this review with their copy and paste comment of 'sorry you have experienced this' which is pathetic. I'm half tempted to upload all the email correspondence admitting Liability for all the faults mentioned above. Easily the worst car buying experience of my life and I certainly won't be buying a car by distance selling ever again. Buyers beware!!!

I purchased a garden furniture set from Laura James which initially appeared to be of excellent quality. However, on the very first day after assembly, one of the chair legs broke during normal use. Assuming this was an isolated manufacturing fault, I contacted Laura James and requested a replacement leg, which they supplied.
A few days later, a far more serious incident occurred. My wife sat on the sofa when another leg suddenly failed, causing the sofa to collapse. As a result, my wife fell and struck her head against the metal leg of our pergola.
I immediately informed Laura James of the incident. Their response was sympathetic, and they offered to send another replacement leg. However, I explained that this was no longer an acceptable solution. Given the repeated structural failures and the injury sustained by my wife, we had completely lost confidence in the safety and quality of the furniture. I therefore requested a full refund, as is my right under the Consumer Rights Act.
I also advised Laura James that, should they refuse to provide a fair resolution, I would have no option but to escalate the matter through Trading Standards and the Small Claims Court.
While awaiting their response regarding the refund request, a third incident occurred. My 15-year-old son sat on one of the chairs and, once again, the leg broke under normal use. Fortunately, he reacted quickly enough to avoid injury. For context, my wife weighs approximately 10 stone and my son approximately 9½ stone, so these failures cannot reasonably be attributed to excessive weight or misuse.
Laura James eventually responded to state that their “Product Specialists” had concluded the damage was caused by over-tightening during assembly. I strongly dispute this allegation. I am a 54-year-old former tradesman with extensive experience assembling flat-pack furniture over many years without issue.
I remain extremely disappointed and concerned by both the apparent safety defects in this furniture and the dismissive handling of a matter that resulted in personal injury.
I am now compiling photographic evidence and documentation in preparation for formal complaints to Trading Standards and, if necessary, proceedings through the Small Claims Court. I will review any further communication from Laura James over the coming week before deciding my next steps.

I ordered a bespoke wardrobe from Online Bedrooms, and as a professional carpenter with 8 years of experience in London, I have never seen such a fundamentally flawed product. This company delivers a pile of poorly cut boards and expects the customer to re-engineer their design mistakes on-site.

The engineering of this unit is a disaster. The internal drawers were manufactured to the full internal width of the carcass without accounting for hinge clearance. As a result, the drawer faces collide directly with the door hinges, making it physically impossible to open them. When raised with customer care, their "technical solution" was to shift the drawers to the left—a physical impossibility since there is zero clearance inside the unit.

Additionally, the main desk surface was supplied significantly shorter than specified, leaving permanent gaps against the walls. Visible panels arrived in mismatched thicknesses, every single internal shelf was factory-cut too long, and essential hardware (including 8 base legs, door hinges, and all handles) was completely missing from the delivery.

To replace the defective, narrow frames and panels now would require a destructive teardown of a fixed unit, ruining hours of precision labor. When confronted with these facts, their Customer Care (Alexandra) officially refused any form of financial compensation or partial refund, hiding behind "company policy" and refusing to take responsibility for their design team's incompetence.

If you are looking for a functional, ready-to-assemble bespoke wardrobe, stay far away from Online Bedrooms. I am now escalating this through my credit provider under a Section 75 breach of contract claim. Avoid at all costs.

one_star_reviews.text: The venue is too large. It's okay, but I'd rather go to the theatres

I am writing to raise a formal complaint about my experience at Nottingham Motorpoint Arena on what was the warmest day I have ever experienced. The conditions inside the venue were unsafe, poorly managed, and showed a complete lack of understanding or care for disabled attendees.

Despite holding a Disability Access Card, this was my first time using it and I was unfamiliar with the process for reserved seating. I stood in the disability area, which was clearly empty with plenty of space. I informed a member of staff that I felt faint due to the extreme heat and the lack of ventilation, yet she showed no interest in helping me, did not ask to see my access card, and made no effort to offer support or guidance.

Because of this, we moved to our standing area — which was overcrowded, tightly packed, and extremely hot, with no noticeable air conditioning. I was sweating profusely and feeling increasingly faint. When I stood at the side on a wooden platform to cool down, another staff member told me I could not stand there and insisted I move back into the densely packed crowd. Again, there was no concern shown for my wellbeing, despite it being visibly obvious that I was struggling.

At no point did any staff member demonstrate training, awareness, or willingness to make reasonable adjustments for a disabled person in distress. The lack of airflow, the extreme heat, and the refusal to allow me to stand somewhere safer directly contributed to my condition worsening. I ultimately had to leave after only 20 minutes of Lily Allen’s performance because I felt so unwell, and I fainted into my friend’s arms shortly after.

This was my first visit to the arena and, based on this experience, it will be my last. The environment was unsafe, the crowding was excessive, and the staff were untrained and dismissive of disability needs — especially concerning given the extreme weather conditions.

Complaint Regarding Discriminatory Treatment in Charity Shop

Dear Sir/Madam,

I visited your charity shop today, 16/05/2026, at approximately 10:15am with my grandmother. What was meant to be a lovely day out together turned into a very upsetting and uncomfortable experience.

When we first entered the shop, everything seemed normal. I was looking for a shoulder bag for my grandmother and then went to the toy section to find a small car for my little one. Afterwards, I returned to my grandmother while she was browsing for trousers.

During this time, I noticed two female members of staff or volunteers — one blonde lady and another with light brown straight hair — repeatedly watching and following my grandmother as though they suspected her of stealing. I stopped and observed the situation myself, and it became very clear that they were closely monitoring her without any reason.

When I questioned the behaviour, one of the ladies responded by saying she could “do what she likes.” I explained that she needed to show respect and understand that we live in a diverse and mixed community where nobody should feel judged or targeted because of their appearance, background, language, or race.

The body language, facial expressions, and overall attitude we received made us feel extremely unwelcome and uncomfortable. My grandmother is 60 years old, and it deeply upset me to see her treated in such a disrespectful manner.

A charitable organisation should be a place where all members of the community feel safe, respected, and welcomed. No one should ever feel discriminated against or unfairly judged while simply shopping.

I hope this matter is taken seriously and addressed appropriately so that no other person or family has to experience this kind of treatment in the future.

Kind regards,

Thank you

I was looking on MoneySuperMarket for car finance and, as soon as car my credit approved, I received a call from Tara Harrison.

From the beginning, I felt Tara was quite pushy. I explained that I hadn’t even decided whether I wanted to go ahead with the vehicle yet and wanted some time to think about it.

When I eventually decided to proceed, I clearly explained that the advertised price included VAT because it was a commercial vehicle. Tara confirmed this was fine and said she would obtain finance quotes. She later came back with approved figures, which I was happy with.

I then received another call from Tara telling me that I had given her the wrong information and that because the vehicle had VAT on it, the figures needed to change and I would need to pay a much larger deposit. I explained that I had specifically told her from the start that the vehicle included VAT and suggested that the call recording be checked. I found her response abrupt and rude, and she accused me of giving incorrect information. I therefore asked for her manager to listen to the call.

Tara told me she was going on leave the next day and that her manager would contact me. No manager ever called. When I later rang for an update, I spoke to one of her colleagues who informed me that the finance company had actually agreed to the original figures and deposit amount, and he sent the paperwork for me to sign.

The following day, Tara called me asking why I had rang while she was on leave. I explained that she had said her manager would call me, but nobody had. She then responded, “Why, could you not afford the larger deposit?” which I found extremely rude and unprofessional.

one_star_reviews.text:
Leaving this to protect others from the poor experience I had with Life and Dream Conversions, which contrasts the overwhelmingly positive reviews visible online.

Initially, I approached Life and Dream conversions for exterior Raptor spray work, a supplied and fitted awning, and a complete off-grid electrical system. The company promotes itself as a "one-stop shop" for full camper conversions, which gave me confidence. Unfortunately, the issues began early on.

The spray job was botched from the start—done in cold weather and clearly not in a proper spray booth. This caused delays and required  further work. Upon collection, sawdust was being blown over and into the van as final work was still happening, which didn’t inspire confidence. Martin dodged questions about the paintwork and told me to inspect it again after cleaning it in a few weeks.

Driving away, I realized the speedometer wasn’t working. Martin later admitted they had removed and discarded the factory-fitted tachograph, which was responsible for the speedo function. More issues quickly emerged—my rear and side doors no longer locked properly or functioned as they had before, compromising security. Martin downplayed the problem, offering no urgency despite £3,000+ worth of equipment now unsecured inside.

I also noticed that the awning looked odd. It turned out the wrong size (2.6m) had been fitted for my L2H2 Ducato. The proper size should have been 3.2m and attached using existing fixings, but instead, they used pretruding brackets drilled in. Kerry acknowledged this mistake and promised a replacement, along with other rectifications, including a respray with a hired booth.

After cleaning the van, I was gutted. The Raptor paintwork was full of gritty patches, missed spots, runs, overspray, visible rust, and damage from tools—far from the protective, durable finish expected. Concerned, I consulted a Raptor specialist who confirmed the poor prep, minimal coating, and substandard results, describing it as nothing more than a "base coat" with inadequate protection.

I had initially been happy with the electrical work, but for peace of mind, I brought in a qualified auto electrician. His verdict: the system was unsafe, lacked basic RCD protection, and had solar panels fitted using wood screws and furniture brackets—dangerously inadequate. He estimated over £2,000 would be needed to correct it. A local garage also laughed at the damaged door mechanisms and poorly reinstalled rear step.

Throughout the process, Martin would pressure me for payments before work had been properly inspected, often citing staff wages, signs of possible cash flow issues. Sadly I fell for these and acted in good faith to help a small business.

Ultimately, I decided not to return the van for rectification. I’d lost all confidence. over £10,000 out of pocket and climbing, with a van that’s unsafe and worse off than when it arrived. I tried to proceed with at least swapping the awning, but Martin never responded on the many occasions I made contact about this. Most disturbingly, he later disputed the professional electrical findings rather than taking responsibility—revealing a dangerous mix of overconfidence and incompetence blurring liens between stupidity and arrogance.

This experience has taught me hard lessons: never pay in full before inspecting work, and be wary of overly glowing reviews—many of which, I suspect, may have been submitted by friends/ employees.

In my opinion, Martin and Life and Dream lack the skills, facilities, and professionalism to deliver safe or high-quality van conversions. The potential danger of poor electrical work should not be understated. Until these serious issues are acknowledged and corrected, I cannot reccomend life and dream conversions.

*UPDATE* Have since had work done to the VAN and our electrician has found concealed cables twisted together throughout the build including the DC to DC Cable which was two Solar Cables strapped together.. Absolute Fraud.

I’m a member who regularly uses both the Sheffield and Nottingham Virgin Active gyms, and the difference in quality between the two is significant.

Sheffield is an excellent facility with outstanding spa amenities — including a hydropool, multiple large sauna and steam rooms, and a well-maintained, spacious wellness area. It genuinely feels like a premium gym experience and justifies the membership cost.

Unfortunately, Nottingham is far below the same standard. The spa facilities are extremely limited: the sauna is very small and has now been closed for over a month, and the steam room is tiny and often overcrowded. The changing rooms are also frequently dirty, and the overall gym feels overcrowded and poorly maintained at peak times.

Given that Virgin Active advertises Nottingham as having spa facilities, this feels quite exaggerated compared to what is actually available on site. Many members I’ve spoken to share the same concerns.

With the recent increase in membership prices, I am seriously reconsidering whether to continue my membership unless significant improvements are made. The Nottingham site feels like it relies too heavily on the “converted station” aesthetic rather than investing in modern, functional facilities that match other Virgin Active gyms.

If Nottingham matched the standard of Sheffield, I would have no hesitation in continuing my membership.

one_star_reviews.text: Not what it once was

A depressing mid 60s Shopping Centre that underwent a multi million redevelopment that didn't work and has had repeated ongoing issues with water ingress through the roof which is also the car park, evidence of this can be seen on the paintwork above shop signs which are peeling and the multitude of small hatches which indicate access points to try and identify where the water is coming from.

The biggest blight is the old nightclub which has been shut for near on 20 years, is riddled with asbestos and no clear plans on what to do or how to demolish it carefully and maintain a working shopping centre.

Since the majority of the big High Street shops have shut down ie BHS, Debenhams, Tesco to name but a few, the Mall has become a pound/discount shoppers paradise. The only lifeline was the onsite Gym opening but this does little in the way of providing a shopping experience and is no more than a revenue stream for Mall.

Many of the large businesses who occupied premises immediately outside The Mall in Blackburn Town Centre such as Mark's & Spencers, have also closed or are closing leaving the town centre a desolate waste ground of second rate charity shops, vape shops and yet more pound shops.

Despite its size its overwhelmingly depressing given there are so many closed units and the many many ongoing maintenance issues despite the huge cost of redeveloping it.

All in all, if I had to travel to a Mall or Shopping Centre, I would rather drive to the Trafford Centre who still have free parking, unlike the Mall, and a vastly superior selection of shops, dining, cinema and other activities OR travel to the Manchester Arndale which offers the same as The Trafford Centre on a slightly smaller scale and has the benefit of Manchester City Centres vibrant hub or bars, restaurants, cinemas, theatres and Museums, numerous car parks, excellent travel links via rail or tram right throughout the day and date, whereas Blackburn has a very poor rail link and although they do have a new Bus Interchange, the lack of buses combined with the length of time to get there make this even less appealing than it normally would be.

The Mall website isnt updated and currently provides zero information in the "Whats Happening in Blackburn" section, most likely because there is nothing happening. The same can be said for the Jobs/Vacancies page, if there truly are 100s of stores then they would be recruiting continually given retail has a high turnover of staff. Does The Mall not employ a Marketing Manager or Assistant? It truly buggers belief that no effort is made to sell themselves as a "major" venue but ut reaffirms my.opinion that if you're own website is not maintained then why bother at all.

The building is plagued by many other maintenance issues such as broken elevators and escalators as well as sliding and manual doors. On one visit there I was witness to an individual relieving themselves of urine and excrement in the public forecourt near Primark, speaks volumes about the clientele.

I'd give The Mall a 3 out of 10 for effort but its sustained lifespan is highly unlikely in the face of considerably better and more attractive venues. Its a mish-mash of new and old that simply fails to deliver on every level and is nothing more than somewhere for the locals and deadbeat to hang around during the day.

Unfortunately I didn't have the best of experiences with this dealership - to say the least.

I purchased a bmw 435d from this garage in the back end of January 2026 with an immaculate 2015 mercedes c250 cdi as p/x with FSH from mercedes specialists. I took the car on a test drive & everything seemed okay. I was offered bottom dollar for my p/x despite being told "it's a lovely car & it's going in their showroom and not to the sister company". It stung but I was too excited to care. By the time I'd got home I realised there was zero in car audio as the amplifier had blown. I had no parking sensors, no Bluetooth, no radio, not even indicators. Silence.

Two garages & three weeks later I received a second hand replacement from ebay while the car was "under warranty". I had to pay for the labour myself & was told the used ebay amplifier "was a gesture of good will" - this was only the start.

Two weeks into ownership the brakes needed replacing with constant screeching on every stop even below 10mph, again I was told this was normal and simply "wear & tear, you need to get it booked in yourself mate" all while still under warranty. The garage was reluctant to pay out on anything & it took A LOT of chasing up as nobody wanted to answer the phone. I will give it to panacea, they did send out new pads - however knowing I had a 435d m sport with the performance brakes I was sent front pads for an X3 & rear pads for a 1 series... Nice one.

Fast forward to april 2026 during my commute I'd been getting constant iDrive warnings advising that the oil was at a critical level. Upon further inspection I realised the car hadn't had a service prior to sale & the filter was saturated & no longer working as it fell apart during a replacement. This left me wondering what else hadn't been checked, after taking it to a reputable BMW specialist in my local area we realised the car had an OBD scanner plugged in & everything reset prior to sale with ZERO work being carried out!! I've had to source my own brakes all round, service the engine and I'm also booked in for an xDrive & transmission service.

£££

After being told by the specialists that I've "well and truly had the piss taken out of me" with the condition of the car AND p/x'ing a car that will have sold for almost double the amount I've been offered, I decided to leave a review sharing my experience to warn others. No names have been mentioned, I'm not bashing their reputation & I'm sugar coating IF ANYTHING! Trying to keep it brief without adding extra issues I've had to fork out for i.e the broken badges on the back they promised to replace & never did, the broken wing vent, one of the door handles missing it's LED light. It's not been great.

I could go on, however it's not worth my time as I've already come to realise the after sales process was more stressful than further putting my hand in my pocket.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this practice based on my recent experience.

I had a private hygienist appointment and, due to an accident causing traffic delays, I contacted the call centre twice to advise that I would be slightly late. Despite this, I arrived at the practice only to be told that the hygienist had not been informed of either call and therefore refused to see me.

Following my complaint, the practice itself acknowledged that the message from the call centre had not been passed on to the clinic. In my view, this internal communication failure contributed directly to the outcome.

What disappointed me even more was the way the complaint was handled. one_star_reviews.text:
My grandad recently stayed here for respite care while my nan was in hospital, and sadly every fear I had about this place became a reality.

Firstly, the room my grandad was placed in was shockingly small — I’ve genuinely stayed in hotel rooms bigger, cleaner, and far more comfortable than this. For somewhere that is supposed to provide care, comfort, and dignity, it felt incredibly disappointing.

My grandad has dementia, which already makes unfamiliar environments distressing, but it was made even worse by the fact that other residents were apparently allowed to walk freely into his room, go through his drawers, and torment him. It got to the point where my grandad was sitting in his chair with his walking stick between his legs because he felt he needed it to “fight off” the other residents who were frightening him. No elderly person should ever feel unsafe in a place they are supposed to be cared for.

He is also hard of hearing, and almost every day we visited, his hearing aid had “gone missing.” We repeatedly found it sitting at reception instead of being returned to him, leaving him unable to hear properly and causing him unnecessary distress and confusion.

One of the most heartbreaking visits was when he kept asking if we had come in the car because he wanted to get in and go home. He repeatedly told us, “the staff don’t do anything for me here.” Hearing that from someone you love is devastating.

We also have video evidence of my grandad in clear distress while staying here, begging to come home and showing how unhappy and uncomfortable he was. However, unlike others, I would never post videos or images showing my grandad’s face publicly in a review because I believe in protecting his identity, dignity, and privacy. His wellbeing should always come before proving a point online.

Thankfully, my grandad has now been moved elsewhere where he will be far more comfortable and properly cared for.

I had actually written a negative review when he first entered this care home because of the way the manager spoke down to me over the phone, along with what felt like a clear conflict of interest. I was asked to remove that review, and I did, purely because I didn’t want it to affect my grandad’s care. Sadly, it’s become very clear that it made no difference anyway.

I also feel it is important to mention that some of the positive reviews posted about this care home are not a true reflection of my grandad’s actual experience. Certain people leaving glowing reviews did not visit my grandad, were not involved in his care, and are only posting positively because the manager is a friend of a family member. That, in itself, shows a serious conflict of interest and makes those reviews feel misleading for families genuinely trying to choose safe and compassionate care for their loved ones.

I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for proper, dignified, and compassionate care for a family member.

My Dad had a 1week stay with no choice in the matter, the care he received was very poor.  He became very scared & distressed as other residents would just walk in his room, he also had items of property go missing.  One day when visiting in the evening we noticed his water jug was empty and the sticker on the jug showed it had been filled the day before, so no fresh water for 24 hours!! The photo below show the cloth I used to wipe the top of his drawers !! Dad went in with a few clothes so that wasn’t from !!

My father in law was unfortunate to spend 7 nights in this building. during his dementia restbite. I cant even call it a care home,due to the lack of care we experienced during our visits. Staff were non existent when needed, we would spend upto 2 hours per visit in his room with the door closed,no members of staff ever checked his wellbeing. Other residents were able to enter his room unchallenged, disturbing him during rest periods. He was frightened and anxious,this was not the care he needed.

I would not recommend this care home under any circumstances based on my grandad’s experience during his respite stay.
From the beginning, there appeared to be a clear lack of person-centred care and communication. My grandad has dementia and became extremely distressed during his stay. Despite being used to seeing family daily and regularly going out with us, I was told I could not take him out, even after this had reportedly been agreed with the social worker. This caused significant confusion and upset for him.

My grandad was frequently isolated in his room and rarely encouraged to spend time in communal areas. Most times I visited, he was alone in silence with no meaningful interaction from staff. Meals were often brought to his room where he ate alone, and other residents repeatedly entered his room, which frightened and distressed him to the point he began locking his own door.

There were continual issues with missing personal belongings and clothing. Items would regularly “reappear” late at night after concerns were raised. I also raised concerns regarding his hearing aid going missing, only to be told my grandad had lost it himself, despite him being unable to independently remove or insert it due to his condition.
I personally had to shave my grandad on occasions, and he informed me he had not been showered. I also pressed the buzzer for assistance on his behalf one day, only for a carer to open the door, say “okay,” and walk away without providing support once I communicated what he needed support with, leaving me to carry this out myself.

Basic care standards also appeared inconsistent. Fresh water was rarely replaced, and the jug was often too heavy for him to safely pour himself a drink. On one occasion, a carer asked if he had already had a cup of tea, accepted his confused response without checking, and walked away. This raises serious concerns around how fluid intake and wellbeing are monitored for vulnerable residents with dementia.

Communication between staff was also contradictory. I was initially told my grandad had a “great night with no concerns,” only to later be informed by management that he had actually had a restless night. Concerns frequently felt passed from “morning staff” to “night staff” without resolution.

I was also told by management that my grandad had been given corned beef pie and then a curry shortly afterwards. I fail to understand why two full meals would be provided one after another to a confused dementia patient.

There were further issues with staff awareness and honesty. On one occasion I was told my grandad was in the dining room, despite me explaining he had become too frightened to leave his room. I was spoken to dismissively, only to then find him exactly where I said he would be.. alone in his bedroom!!

Even simple concerns were ignored. My grandad had a television in his room with no remote control for a prolonged period, despite this being raised multiple times. Every visit, I would find him sat alone in silence until I manually turned the television on for him.
I have video evidence of my grandad expressing in his own words that he was unhappy and frightened during his stay. However, unlike others, I will not publicly share vulnerable footage of my grandad online.

I am grateful the appropriate authorities have been made aware of the concerns surrounding his stay. Families place enormous trust in care homes to protect vulnerable loved ones with dignity, compassion, and proper care. Unfortunately, based on our experience, I do not feel that happened here.

Update – June 2026

I am updating this review because the matter has now reached a very unfortunate outcome. Losing my deposit is the complete opposite of what I hoped for when I amended my original review.

I reserved two flats at Queens Court through CityRise in February 2024, with an expected completion date of Q4 2024. Instead, completion was pushed back repeatedly over two years — from Q4 2024 to Q1 2025, then March, June, July, August and October 2025. The development was not ready when promised, and for long periods valuations could not even be carried out as a result.

I first reviewed CityRise on Trustpilot in March 2025 after becoming frustrated with the delays. Following that review, a director personally appealed to me, apologised on the developer’s behalf, said the delays were the developer’s responsibility, and assured me that CityRise was on my side. Based on those assurances, I amended my review and continued to be patient.

I did everything asked of me. I renewed mortgage offers when they expired due to delays, paid repeated fees, agreed to renegotiate after the properties were down-valued, and confirmed again and again that I wanted to complete.

In March 2026, we were informed by our solicitor that completion could not take place because the developer’s solicitor had still not answered key lender enquiries, meaning the lender could not release funds. The delays continued, and the developer’s side remained unresponsive.

I raised written complaints with CityRise about the delays and the financial impact of the expired mortgage offers. After weeks of chasing and waiting, the developer decided to terminate the contracts and forfeit my deposit.

What disappoints me most is that the CityRise director who once asked me to change my review and assured me they had my back has remained silent. Their aftersales contact told me to negotiate with the developer myself. When I contacted the developer, I was simply told to go through the developer’s lawyers.

This has been the worst financial decision I have ever made. I had around £35,000 tied up for over two years, plus roughly £10,000 in related costs, including mortgage fees, valuation fees, legal fees and other expenses. I was always willing and able to proceed, and I never refused to complete.

Purchasing an off-plan property through CityRise has been a disaster for me. Based on my experience, I would strongly urge anyone considering it to think very carefully before proceeding.

Seems as though the ownership doesn't seem to care as much as they once did, and looking at other recent reviews it's sad to see that others feel the same way. Once my favourite shop, now I wouldn't even recommend it.

Smoak Chorlton used to be, without question, one of the best coffee shops in Manchester. The coffee was consistently exceptional - genuinely unmatched - and it was the kind of place you’d happily go out of your way for.

Sadly, after the huge turnover of staff, it’s become completely inconsistent. I went to Kiosk on Lapwing today because I genuinely can’t trust that I’ll get a decent coffee at Smoak anymore. The quality has fallen off a cliff, and the new staff seem incapable of making coffee anywhere near the standard this place built its reputation on.

What really summed it up was the conversation I had while at Kiosk. I mentioned to the barista that I’d stopped going to my local because of how bad Smoak had become, and another customer nearby immediately jumped into the conversation to say they’d also abandoned Smoak after receiving a horrendous coffee that very morning and had switched to Kiosk instead.

News travels fast, and it honestly feels like what was once considered one of Manchester’s greatest coffee spots has now become known for how dramatically downhill it’s gone. It’s disappointing more than anything, because this place used to set the standard.

I would strongly advise anyone to avoid Automotive Finesse at all costs. After a recent minor accident, my insurance company (Admiral) directed me to this garage via Auxillis. The front bumper was replaced, but the service that followed was a nightmare.
Once the car was returned, I immediately noticed major electronic faults: the parking sensors stopped working, and the start-stop system failed (this was not an issue before the accident and even after the accident). Automotive Finesse tried to fob me off multiple times—first, they claimed my newly fitted battery needed replacing. Then I returned a 2nd time and they said that the battery wasn’t correct for the car. Then I took it back a third time and they were trying to argue these were pre-existing issues. I took the car to an independent mechanic who confirmed that there were no faults before the car entered the garage, the battery was tested and 100% working and correct for my car. Instead, Automotive Finesse had simply misaligned the sensors during the repair. To add insult to injury, the front grill wasn’t even fitted correctly—it was just reattached on with double-sided tape which has been discovered by my independent garage.
All of this has cost me personal time and money. I would strongly urge anyone to stay away from this garage. Poor workmanship, lack of accountability, and a complete waste of time. Avoid them if you value your car and your peace of mind.

This has been one of the most frustrating and stressful experiences I have ever had with a professional service. I instructed Right Legal Group to deal with my late father’s estate, expecting guidance, support and regular communication during an already difficult time. Unfortunately, the reality was the complete opposite.

Emails frequently went unanswered, phone calls were not returned, and I was left constantly chasing for updates. The lack of communication was so poor that I often had to contact HMRC and the Probate Registry myself to find out what was happening with the case because I could not get the information I needed from the firm.

The ongoing failure to respond caused unnecessary delays, prolonged the process and added significant stress at a time when I was already dealing with the loss of my father. My father specifically wanted me to use this firm so that I would have professional support and less to worry about. Instead, I found myself doing much of the chasing and administration myself while struggling to obtain even basic updates.

I raised a formal complaint with the company regarding the service I received, but this did not change my overall experience.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this firm. If communication, responsiveness and client care are important to you, I would strongly suggest looking elsewhere.

After my Dad passed away we were devastated and the greif absolutely consumed us. My Dad did not leave a will so we used right probate to complete the probate during a time we physically couldn't.

We put our trust in this company and they did nothing but lie, send private documents to wrong addresses, offer a service they could not provide, delay the whole process and the communication was beyond poor.

During a time we should have been greiving they stole that from us with their beyond poor customer service.

I requested a reduction in fees due to the inadequate service we received. They offered a measly £250 for 22 months of turmoil which they have upheld as "reasonable". Just beyond disgusting!

I will be taking this further and going to a small claims. This isn't about money its about treating customers who are greiving fairly and not taking advantage.

I will be donating anything received to St. Peter's Hospice which is a company that cared deeply and supported my Dad with dignity and respect. Something Right Probate could learn from.

Avoid at all cost!

We visited today for the first time and, as soon as we walked in, we were greeted by a rude man who, judging by the other bad reviews, I'm assuming was the owner. He said "hello" with no follow-up and looked at us confused, as if we weren't allowed to be there. It seemed as though he wasn't going to say anything else, so I pointed to an empty table and asked if we could sit there. He then laughed and said "no" before pausing and saying that some tables were reserved - although there were no reserved signs on them, otherwise I obviously wouldn't have asked. He then bluntly pointed to a specific table in the corner and told us we could sit there. Bear in mind there were only three other tables occupied when we arrived, so the whole thing felt unnecessarily pedantic.

Throughout our visit, we noticed a clear difference in the level of service given to other customers. Having read the other reviews, there seems to be a common theme that if you haven't booked or aren't a regular, you don't get the same treatment. The waitresses were lovely and we couldn't fault them, but the service from this man was extremely patronising.

Considering the place was more than half empty, the service was incredibly slow and we were there for an hour and a half. We repeatedly struggled to get any attention; multiple times he clearly saw us but chose not to come over. Meanwhile, he was checking on other tables that had arrived after us, asking if everything was okay and offering more food and drinks - all while our plates were empty and stacked ready to be collected.

At the end, when we asked if we could pay, he looked almost disgusted and pointed to the till saying "it's over there" as though that should have been obvious, despite the fact we'd never been before. The waitresses who had served us throughout had also been carrying card machines, so we assumed you could pay at the table like in most food places.

Overall, although the food itself was nice, the atmosphere and service were very unwelcoming and made us feel uncomfortable from start to finish. I definitely won't be returning and wouldn't recommend it to anyone - unless you're a regular, of course. I had a better experience at the Co-op down the road.

If I could give zero stars, I absolutely would. My experience with Trust Motor Centre LTD has been nothing short of a nightmare and completely ruined my first car-buying experience.

I bought a car from them just over a year ago and within a month I had to take it to Citroën for major repairs. After doing some research, I discovered they have a scrapyard full of junk cars right next to their small dealership, which should have been my first red flag. I refused to let them “fix” my car because Citroën offered brand new parts with a full-year warranty, while Trust Motor Centre claimed they could fix everything for £1,600, which would not have even covered half the work required. I am certain they would have sourced parts from scrap cars, so I would strongly advise anyone not to trust them to repair your vehicle.

Citroën confirmed the clutch and flywheel were completely worn, rusty and corroded, damage that could never have happened in under 1,000 miles of normal driving, especially since the car is an automatic. Despite this, the dealer tried to blame it on my driving. They also installed faulty ABS sensors to hide dashboard warnings, and once these were replaced, multiple serious faults appeared.

The car should never have passed an MOT. It had:

Extremely worn brake pads and badly lipped discs

Congealed and clogged brake fluid

Completely perished exhaust mounts

Completely shot suspension

All of this made the car unsafe and unroadworthy.

I had to go through Trading Standards and AA mediation just to get the £1,600 they claimed it would cost to repair, even though the total bill came to nearly £6,000. This whole ordeal caused months of stress and anxiety and seriously affected my mental health.

I spent nearly £40 on two biothane collars at Crufts, paying a premium specifically for the matte-black hardware aesthetic. After less than 2 months of incredibly light use (only clipping a lead on occasionally for quick garden toilet breaks as harnesses are used for walks), the black coating completely flaked off, exposing the raw metal underneath.

​When I contacted customer service, they refused a refund, claiming the degradation is "normal wear and tear" and that because the collar still physically holds together, it isn't faulty.

​By their logic, if you bought a piece of gold-plated jewellery and all the gold flaked off to reveal cheap green metal within weeks, you shouldn’t complain because "it still fits on your finger and functions as a ring."

​The company clearly does not understand the Consumer Rights Act 2015. Under Section 9, a product's appearance, finish, and durability are part of its statutory quality. A dog collar finish that disintegrates under normal contact with a standard dog lead is inherently unfit for purpose.

​Because they flatly refused to honour my legal rights or even provide a prepaid returns label, I escalated the matter to my bank. After reviewing the evidence and the company's emails, it was ruled in my favour and the full amount was provided back via a chargeback.

​Ditsty Pet needs to rethink both the quality of their products and their understanding of how UK consumer law works. Save your money and buy a biothane collar elsewhere (you can get the same collars on Etsy for about £8) from a business that actually values quality and respects its customers' legal rights.

Update to their response:
​The claim about my review history is completely false; a simple click on my Google profile shows my other reviews are 5 stars.

​More importantly, notice how they completely omit the fact that my bank formally investigated this case, reviewed our email chain, and legally ruled in my favour, forcing a full reversal of the funds. A bank does not claw back money from a merchant for a "difficult customer" over simple "wear and tear"—they do it when a business has breached consumer law.

​I declined a replacement because I had no desire to receive more sub-standard hardware where the finish flakes off in two months.

Resorting to false claims about a customer's history changes nothing. My bank legally vindicated my claim, and no amount of public deflecting or calling paying customers "difficult" changes the fact that your product finish failed basic durability standards under the Consumer Rights Act.

one_star_reviews.text: To be honest, it's just easier to die than come here

Absolute disgrace of an A&E department.

As a medical professional myself, I was appalled by both the staff and the way this department was run.

I attended A&E just before midnight on 9th June with chest pains. The lady on reception, whose name I didn’t catch but who was blonde and wore glasses, was one of the rudest members of staff I have ever encountered. The triage nurse, who I believe may have been called Leanne (although I’m not 100% certain), was equally unpleasant. She appeared completely uninterested, miserable, and incapable of even the slightest smile. Despite being the only person triaging patients, she spent time standing around talking to other members of staff while patients continued to wait.

I work within private healthcare, and you would never see nurses standing around chatting when the department is busy.

Before attending, I had already spoken to NHS 111 regarding my chest pain. Despite this, it took over an hour before I was triaged. Chest pain should be assessed as a priority, yet a patient with shoulder pain and another with a suspected sprained ankle were seen before me. We approached reception to check that my details had been recorded correctly and to ask what was happening, but the receptionist was dismissive and rude. She stated that she was not medically trained. While that may be true, it does not take medical training to understand that chest pain is a higher priority than a suspected sprained ankle.

Shortly after complaining, I was finally called through.

What was even more concerning was the way an elderly gentleman was treated while I was waiting. He was clearly hard of hearing and struggled to walk. The triage nurse was shouting at him and speaking to him in a rude and impatient manner, instructing him to sit on the black chairs. Around 30 minutes later, the receptionist was shouting for him because his taxi had arrived. She then aggressively questioned why he was sitting where he was. The gentleman explained that he had been told to sit there, to which she responded, “No they didn’t, no one would tell you to sit there.”

At that point I stood up because the way he was being spoken to was genuinely awful. I told her that yes, he had been told to sit there, and that the nurse had spoken to him in exactly the same manner. Only then did she apologise to him.

As an audiologist myself, I fully understand the difference between raising your voice to help someone hear and outright shouting at them with a rude and dismissive attitude. What I witnessed was not an attempt to communicate with a hearing-impaired patient; it was simply poor behaviour.

I also found it ironic that there were signs throughout the department stating there is “no excuse for abusing staff”, yet the only abusive behaviour I witnessed came from members of staff themselves. In any other profession, speaking to vulnerable and elderly people in this way would lead to disciplinary action.

An utterly disappointing experience. It’s a shame private hospitals don’t have an A&E department, I’d rather go bankrupt that witness and experience that again.

Dear Goyard London Leadership Team,

I am writing to formally raise a serious complaint regarding my recent visit to your London store — an experience that was not only distressing but handled with a level of dismissiveness and disrespect wholly unbefitting a brand of Goyard's standing.

During my visit, I sat on one of the in-store sofas, unaware that it was wet. There were no warning signs placed on or around the sofa, and no member of staff alerted me to its condition beforehand. As a result, my clothing was left visibly soaked — in your store, in full view of other customers.

When I brought this to the attention of a staff member, rather than receiving a genuine apology or any meaningful attempt to assist, I was met with a dismissive and frankly rude response. I was told, words to the effect of: "It just happened, we cannot do anything about it — you were supposed to sit on it at a time when we were going to do something about it."

I want to be absolutely clear about what that response communicates: that I, the customer, am at fault for sitting on a sofa inside your store. That is not an explanation. That is not an apology. That is blame-shifting — and it is unacceptable at any level of retail, let alone at a house with Goyard's heritage and reputation.

Further to this, I had been stopped at the entrance and informed that drinks were not permitted in the store — a rule I respected without question. Yet I observed other customers inside freely carrying drinks, with no intervention from staff whatsoever. The selective and inconsistent application of your own rules only added to the sense that certain customers are treated very differently from others.

Most troublingly of all, after I raised my concerns with your store manager and left the premises, I was made aware that she was laughing about the incident. A customer walked out of your store humiliated, with wet clothing, after a hazard your team failed to address — and the response from management was amusement. This is not a lapse in service standards. This is a fundamental failure of basic human respect.

I want to start by saying that the staff in Thrive are always friendly and welcoming, and I am usually greeted with a smile. However, there needs to be a serious conversation about the quality of the food and beverages, as well as the cleanliness of the gym and the standard of the equipment.

Firstly, several members of staff clearly require basic training in how to operate the coffee machines properly, especially considering coffee is priced at £4+ each. On a regular basis, I am served coffee that is dangerously hot, to the point where I have burnt my mouth drinking it and sometimes cannot even hold the cup comfortably without burning my hands. Often, the coffee is not cool enough to drink until 20 minutes after it has been served. Not only is this unpleasant, but overheating the milk and coffee also burns the drink itself and ruins the quality.

There have been multiple occasions where I have politely returned my coffee and asked for it to be remade, only to be met with poor attitudes and visible frustration from staff.

In addition, staff should be able to distinguish between basic drinks such as a latte, cappuccino, and flat white. At the moment, the drinks are inconsistent and often incorrect. These are fundamental standards for any café, particularly one charging £4+ for a coffee

There also appears to be inconsistent pricing, with one member of staff regularly charging customers different amounts for the same items. This creates confusion and gives the impression of poor management and lack of clear procedures.

I understand that Thrive is operated by Total Fitness, but something urgently needs to be done regarding both the quality and temperature of the drinks before someone is seriously injured , particularly given that children are often around the café area.

The food quality is also extremely disappointing. Aside from the croissants, which appear to be pre-bought frozen products, very little on the menu is enjoyable and is regularly inedible. This is a real shame because the café itself has huge potential to be a modern, trendy, and enjoyable social space for members. Unfortunately, the current standard is far below expectations.

More broadly, the gym facilities themselves are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. The gym has over 3,000 members, yet there appears to be very little investment in maintaining or improving the changing rooms and equipment. The changing rooms are consistently dirty, outdated, and have not been refurbished in over 20 years. In addition, equipment is frequently broken or out of service.

From conversations I have overheard in the changing rooms and around the gym, I know I am far from the only member who feels this way.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and acted upon rather than dismissed. At a minimum, staff need proper barista training, consistent pricing guidance, improved food standards, and greater attention paid to cleanliness and equipment maintenance. Until these issues are addressed, I cannot justify spending money at Thrive and would not feel comfortable in recommending a membership to others.

I visited this branch today at around 12:55pm to purchase a GRP cabinet and an isolator, and I experienced some of the worst customer service I have ever received from any trade supplier.

The young member of staff who came out from the office to serve us was rude, impatient, dismissive and completely uninterested in helping. As we were discussing our requirements, he started demanding technical details. Since I am not an electrician, I called our electrician to get the correct information. While I was on the phone trying to obtain and relay the answers, he repeatedly attempted to rush me through the conversation despite there being no queue and no obvious reason for such behaviour.

Instead of helping us identify the correct products, he scribbled down an email address and effectively told us to email everything over because there are “thousands of options.” The way this was delivered was arrogant, condescending and borderline insulting. He spoke as if customers should already know every technical specification before walking into the branch.

What is the purpose of having a trade counter if customers are simply going to be pushed towards an email address? We travelled from another town to visit the branch specifically so we could discuss our requirements face-to-face and receive guidance. If we wanted to send an email, we could have done that from our office. The company advertises email addresses everywhere. We came to the branch because we expected knowledgeable staff and customer service. Instead, we were treated like a nuisance.

This individual seemed far more interested in getting rid of us than helping us. In all my years dealing with builders’ merchants and electrical wholesalers, I have rarely encountered someone so unhelpful and lacking in basic customer service skills.

Our group of companies has spent thousands of pounds with this business over the years. We are also currently involved in a new development project and had intended to purchase a substantial amount of electrical materials through this company. Following today’s experience, that will not be happening. They have not only lost a major order, they have lost any future business from us. Frankly, after the way we were treated, I would rather pay more elsewhere than spend another penny in this branch.

If this is the standard of service being provided, management should be extremely concerned. One member of staff has managed to destroy years of goodwill and completely eliminate any confidence we had in this branch.

Avoid.
